Overview
items.text:
BetterPy uses CalVer (Calendar Versioning) with the format: YYYY.MM.PATCH[-channel.build] (MM is zero-padded)

This versioning scheme provides: - Clear timeline visibility for releases - Natural alignment with monthly release cadence - Support for multiple release channels (stable, beta, dev) - Simple bugfix tracking

items.title: Base Format: YYYY.MM.PATCH
items.text:
• YYYY: 4-digit year
  • MM: Month without leading zero (1-12)
  • PATCH: Bugfix/patch number (starts at 0)

items.title: Channel Suffix: -channel.build
items.text: Optional suffix for pre-release and development builds: - channel: Release channel name (dev, beta, alpha, rc) - build: Build number or timestamp

items.title: Stable Releases
items.text:
Monthly production releases following calendar months.

Format: YYYY.MM.0

Examples: - 2026.01.0 - January 2026 release - 2026.02.0 - February 2026 release - 2026.12.0 - December 2026 release

When to use: - Regular monthly feature releases - Production-ready code - Published to default channel in JetBrains Marketplace

items.title: Bugfix Releases
items.text:
Patch releases for urgent fixes within a monthly cycle.

Format: YYYY.MM.PATCH (where PATCH > 0)

Examples: - 2026.01.1 - First bugfix for January 2026 - 2026.01.2 - Second bugfix for January 2026

When to use: - Critical bug fixes - Security patches - Hot fixes between monthly releases

items.title: Development Builds
items.text:
Unstable development snapshots with timestamps.

Format: YYYY.MM.0-dev.YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS

Examples: - 2026.01.0-dev.20260115-143000 - 2026.02.0-dev.20260203-091500

When to use: - Automated CI builds - Feature branch testing - Internal development testing - Published to dev channel

items.title: Beta Releases
items.text:
Pre-release versions for wider testing before stable release.

Format: YYYY.MM.0-beta.N

Examples: - 2026.01.0-beta.1 - First beta - 2026.01.0-beta.2 - Second beta

When to use: - Feature complete but needs testing - User acceptance testing - Published to beta channel

items.title: Alpha Releases
items.text:
Early pre-release versions for initial testing.

Format: YYYY.MM.0-alpha.N

Examples: - 2026.01.0-alpha.1 - 2026.01.0-alpha.2

When to use: - Early feature testing - Breaking changes testing - Published to alpha channel

items.title: Release Candidates
items.text:
Final testing before stable release.

Format: YYYY.MM.0-rc.N

Examples: - 2026.01.0-rc.1 - 2026.01.0-rc.2

When to use: - Final testing phase - No new features, only bug fixes - Published to rc channel

items.title: IntelliJ Marketplace Channels
items.text:
The build system automatically routes versions to appropriate channels:

Version Pattern Channel Visibility 2026.01.0 default All users 2026.01.1 default All users 2026.01.0-beta.X beta Beta testers 2026.01.0-alpha.X alpha Alpha testers 2026.01.0-rc.X rc RC testers 2026.01.0-dev.X dev Developers only

items.title: Version Management Script
items.text: Use scripts/version.sh for automated version management:

items.title: Show Current Version
items.text: ./scripts/version.sh current

items.title: Preview Next Version
items.text:
# Next stable monthly release
./scripts/version.sh next --channel=stable

# Next bugfix
./scripts/version.sh next --channel=bugfix

# Next dev build
./scripts/version.sh next --channel=dev

# Next beta
./scripts/version.sh next --channel=beta

items.title: Bump Version
items.text:
# Bump to next stable release
./scripts/version.sh bump --channel=stable

# Bump to next bugfix
./scripts/version.sh bump --channel=bugfix

# Create dev build
./scripts/version.sh bump --channel=dev

# Create beta release
./scripts/version.sh bump --channel=beta

The script automatically: - Updates gradle.properties - Creates a backup (.bak file) - Uses current date for stable/dev versions - Increments build numbers for beta/alpha/rc

items.text:

items.text:

# 3. Create second beta

items.title: Git Tags
items.text: Tag format matches version format: - Stable: 2026.01.0 - Bugfix: 2026.01.1 - Beta: 2026.01.0-beta.1 - Dev: Not typically tagged (ephemeral)

items.title: Migration from SemVer
items.text:
If migrating from SemVer (e.g., 0.0.1):

  1. Choose appropriate CalVer version based on current date
  2. Update gradle.properties
  3. Update CHANGELOG.md with new section
  4. Tag the transition commit

Example: 

# New: 2026.01.0 (January 2026)
./scripts/version.sh bump --channel=stable

items.title: Best Practices
items.text:
1. Monthly Cadence: Aim for stable releases at the start of each month
  2. Bugfix Windows: Reserve patches for critical fixes only
  3. Beta Testing: Use beta channel for 1-2 weeks before stable
  4. Dev Builds: Automate in CI for every commit to main
  5. Changelog: Always update CHANGELOG.md before tagging
  6. Testing: Test beta/rc thoroughly before promoting to stable
  7. Communication: Announce releases with clear channel information

items.title: FAQ
items.text:
Q: What if I need to release twice in one month? A: Use patch versions (e.g., 2026.01.0, then 2026.01.1 if needed)

Q: Can I skip months? A: Yes! If no release in February, go directly to 2026.03.0 in March

Q: How do I handle multiple features in development? A: Use dev builds (-dev.timestamp) or feature branches with beta releases

Q: What about breaking changes? A: Document in CHANGELOG.md and consider using beta cycle for user feedback

Q: Can I use week numbers instead of months? A: Yes, modify the script to use YYYY.WW.PATCH format (week of year)

items.title: Private module import inspection
items.text:
Since 2026.06.0 · Maturity Stable

This inspection reports imports from private implementation modules when the imported symbol is already available from the public package API.

items.title: Example
items.text:
from package._internal import User

If package.__all__ exports User, BetterPy suggests importing from package instead:

from package import User

When the symbol is not exported yet, the inspection can also make the symbol public by updating the package __all__, adding the re-export import, and rewriting matching private imports outside that package.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The inspection helps keep callers on public package APIs.
  • Imports inside the exporting package are left alone, so implementation modules can still use private package internals.
  • It is gated by the Private module import inspection setting under Settings | BetterPy | Code Quality & Safety | Import Inspections.

items.title: Pytest parametrized case run gutter icon
items.text:
Since 2026.06.0 · Maturity Incubating · Issues [PY-88558](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/PY-88558)[PY-46650](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/PY-46650)

This feature adds run gutter icons for individual pytest.mark.parametrize cases.

items.title: How to use it
items.text:
Put each parametrized case on its own line, then use the gutter run icon beside the case to run only that pytest node.

Parametrized TestRun Target 
import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [
    "admin",
    "guest",
])
def test_role(value):
    assert value

test_roles.py::test_role[guest]

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The line marker appears only when BetterPy can infer the exact pytest case ID.
  • Explicit ids from ids=[...] and pytest.param(..., id="...") are supported.
  • The feature is gated by the Pytest parametrized case run gutter icon setting under Settings | BetterPy | Testing (Pytest) | Parametrize.

This release ships BetterPy's mock-patching and mock-typing tooling in stable builds, previously available only in dev builds: mock type inference for Mock/MagicMock/AsyncMock with spec/spec_set support, mock.patch target navigation and mock.patch.object attribute completion/navigation, and an inspection for unresolved attributes on specced mocks. The pytest fixture engine also got a significant navigation/inspection performance pass for large repositories.

items.title: Mock assertion methods
items.text:
Since 2026.08.0 · Maturity Stable
  • Mock assertion methods are now available, resolving unittest.mock assertion methods (assert_called_once_with, assert_any_call, and similar) without enabling the broader dev-only mock type provider, and correctly resolve pytest-mock's Mock, MagicMock, and AsyncMock aliases to their unittest.mock classes for consistent spec/spec_set typing.

items.title: Mock type provider
items.text:
Since 2026.08.0 · Maturity Stable
  • Mock type inference infers the type of Mock, MagicMock, and AsyncMock construction and of patch/patch.object return values, propagating spec/spec_set classes (including lists of protocols) through mock attribute and method access, return_value, and helper functions that return a mock, so calls on properly specced mocks resolve like calls on the real target.

items.title: Mock patch reference
items.text:
Since 2026.08.0 · Maturity Stable
  • Mock patch reference resolves and navigates the dotted target string passed to mock.patch(...), including static segments of f-string targets, and lets Go to Declaration jump from a mock.patch.object(target, "attribute") attribute string to the real attribute on the target class.

items.title: Mock patch object attribute completion
items.text:
Since 2026.08.0 · Maturity Stable
  • Mock patch object attribute completion completes the attribute name in mock.patch.object(target, "attribute") calls based on the target's inferred type.

items.title: Mock unresolved reference inspection
items.text:
Since 2026.08.0 · Maturity Stable
  • Mock unresolved reference inspection flags attribute reads and writes on specced Mock/MagicMock/AsyncMock instances that don't resolve against the spec/spec_set class, catching typos that would otherwise be silently accepted by Mock's auto-attribute behavior.

items.title: Pytest hooks
items.text:
Since 2026.07.0 · Maturity Incubating

items.title: Jump to pytest node in test tree
items.text:
Since 2026.07.0 · Maturity Incubating

Jump to pytest node in test tree selects the matching node in the active pytest test tree for the test at the editor caret.

items.title: How to use it
items.text: Place the caret inside a pytest test function or class, then run BetterPy: Jump to Test Tree Node from the editor context menu or intention list.

items.title: When it helps
items.text: Use this feature after a pytest run when the editor is focused but you want to inspect the matching result node, failure state, or surrounding suite in the test tree.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The action is available only when there is an active non-empty test tree.
  • The feature is gated by the Jump to pytest node in test tree setting under Settings | BetterPy | Testing (Pytest) | Test Tree & Navigation.

items.title: Toggle pytest skip from test tree
items.text:
Since 2026.07.0 · Maturity Incubating

Toggle pytest skip from test tree adds or removes @pytest.mark.skip for selected pytest nodes.

items.title: How to use it
items.text: Select a pytest function, class, module, or pytest explorer entry, then run BetterPy: Toggle Pytest Skip from the context menu.

items.title: When it helps
items.text: Use this action when triaging failures from the test results view and you want to skip or unskip the affected test without navigating manually through the project tree.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Function selections toggle the marker on that function.
  • Class and module selections toggle the marker at the matching scope.
  • The feature is gated by the Toggle pytest skip from test tree setting under Settings | BetterPy | Testing (Pytest) | Test Tree & Navigation.

items.title: Copy method annotations from parent
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating

Copy missing type annotations from a parent method into an overriding method. This is useful when subclass methods intentionally keep the same signature but were written without annotations.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on an overriding method and use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "Copy type annotations from parent".

items.title: Example
items.text:
class Handler:
    def handle(self, event: Event) -> Result:
        ...


class AuditHandler(Handler):
    def handle(self, event):
        ...

becomes:

class AuditHandler(Handler):
    def handle(self, event: Event) -> Result:
        ...

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Copying missing parameter annotations.
  • Copying missing return annotations.
  • Keeping existing child annotations when they are already present.
  • Adding imports required by copied annotation names.
  • Rewriting common alias imports so the resulting annotation resolves in the child file.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Methods with no typed parent method.
  • Signature shapes that do not line up with the parent method.
  • Blindly overwriting annotations already present on the child.
  • Applying a fix when import or name conflicts need explicit review.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The intention can be used directly, and the overridden-method inspection can offer it as a quick-fix.
  • The feature is gated by the Copy method annotations from parent setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Type Editing.

items.title: 🐛 Bug Fixes
items.text:
• Pytest fixture documentation falls back to rendering the fixture's own docstring when its return type can't be enriched with field/value info, instead of showing no documentation at all.
  • Pytest fixture editor integration resolves fixture override imports for types imported under TYPE_CHECKING or other conditional blocks and for classes declared locally in a pytest plugin module, generates fixture overrides as pass-throughs that preserve the parent fixture's behavior and avoid recursion, and avoids nested blocking reads when resolving fixture override hierarchies during indexing.
  • Class implementations code vision avoids duplicate and stale results when resolving import aliases.
  • Docstring Example Rendering renders the underlying class docstring for class aliases assigned from a class reference or class instantiation.

items.title: 🚀 Features
items.text:
• Pytest fixture intelligence now extends PyCharm's built-in pytest support with BetterPy's own fixture index and resolver. This improves fixture understanding across conftest.py, plugin modules, autouse fixtures, fixture overrides, string-based fixture references, and dynamic fixture providers such as register_fixture.
  • Pytest fixture inspections and navigation are now powered by that resolver. BetterPy can highlight unused fixtures, direct fixture imports, fixture-scope narrowing, uninjected fixture references, no-op @pytest.mark.usefixtures decorators, redundant fixture imports, and pytest_plugins declarations in non-root conftest.py files, while also making pytest identifiers available in Search Everywhere and fixture Find Usages.
  • Pytest fixture hierarchy support makes fixtures behave more like ordinary overridden Python members. You can jump from an overriding fixture to the broader-scope fixture it shadows, and gutter markers show which narrower-scope fixtures override the current fixture.
  • Pytest fixture editor integration makes fixture names act more like normal Python symbols: fixture parameters can resolve to the fixture definition pytest would choose, fixture-name completion uses the visible fixture set for the current file, and Go to Implementation can list narrower-scope fixture overrides.
  • Pytest fixture Quick Documentation and type inference build on the same fixture model to cover cases tracked by the linked PyCharm issues, including richer fixture value types, unresolved or uninjected fixture references, and basic checks that a test or fixture parameter annotation matches the resolved fixture return type.
  • Pytest parametrization helpers add intentions for creating and maintaining @pytest.mark.parametrize decorators, converting values to and from pytest.param(...), and running individual parametrized cases from the editor gutter.
  • Pytest test-tree actions add copyable node IDs, editor-to-test-tree navigation, skip toggling from the test tree, and a debug-logging run variant for the selected pytest node.
  • Pytest test-writing helpers add Generate-menu actions for new tests, fixtures, and pytest hooks, plus editor intentions for toggling @pytest.mark.skip and wrapping statements with pytest.raises(...).
  • Inherited attribute documentation shows an ancestor attribute's docstring when an overriding class attribute has no local documentation, preserving useful Quick Documentation across class hierarchies.

items.title: 🐛 Bug Fixes
items.text:
• Pytest fixture documentation, already available in stable, shows consumer-scoped fixture variants and follows static fixture pass-throughs in Quick Documentation, renders correctly for class-based fixture containers, and stays compatible with newer PyCharm platform versions.
  • Pytest fixture editor integration suppresses feature nudges while focus is outside the editor.
  • Class implementations code vision includes specced mocks in class inlays, ignores inferred protocol method return types, mirrors native protocol library implementation behavior, and keeps code-vision navigation constrained to the intended editor split.
  • Go to target presentation mirrors native protocol library implementation behavior for library protocols.
  • Test/Production editor tabs preserves the active split and placement when moving files right, avoids duplicate splits, keeps navigation history intact, guards editor tab pin checks, creates a split when needed for navigation routing, guards action event file lookups with read access, honors pytest's configured collection naming, and applies workspace-aware source roots consistently.
  • Property usages code vision stabilizes usage-count recording and keeps code-vision navigation constrained to the intended editor split.
  • Module assignment usages code vision keeps code-vision navigation constrained to the intended editor split.
  • Constant should be Final inspection avoids unsafe Final annotations for literal regular-expression values, reuses existing and re-exported imports instead of adding duplicates, preserves literal builtin types and quote qualifiers, collapses homogeneous tuple types, normalizes generated import order, and supports newer PyCharm collection type APIs.
  • Shadowing stdlib module inspection no longer rewrites existing references when renaming through the dialog, and avoids subclassing a final platform file-action class.
  • Missing None annotation inspection avoids emitting a duplicate quick-fix action.
  • Docstring Example Rendering renders reStructuredText docstring examples and preserves field lists when rendering fenced code.
  • Copy method annotations from parent avoids duplicate actions, prefers existing qualified imports, normalizes import insertion order, guards against stale PSI when reading the copy plan, and recognizes stub and implementation modules as the same module identity.
  • Copy with imports avoids resolving shadowed names when copying imports.
  • Generate class actions keeps generated names selected and normalizes generated import order.
  • Export symbol to target avoids PSI reads outside read access, applies workspace-aware source roots, and uses pytest's configured naming when checking feature guards.
  • Introduce Parameter Object (refactoring and MCP tool) respects disabled feature gates and reuses existing Python imports when generating parameter objects.
  • Make parameter mandatory preserves override propagation.
  • Make parameter optional preserves type-only optional declarations.
  • Change visibility avoids running usage previews on the EDT and uses pytest's configured naming when checking feature guards.
  • Attribute docstring renders module-assignment docstring examples correctly.
  • Dict access avoids stale PSI after intention edits.
  • Top-level extract function prevents refactoring-action crashes and tolerates a missing Python extract handler.
  • Message console filter links constructor-style class representations in the console.
  • Python navigation bar renders dunder methods correctly in navbar breadcrumbs.
  • Use actual test outcome uses pytest's configured naming when checking feature guards.
  • Analytics follows the IDE usage-statistics setting by default and no longer sends an opt-out event.

items.text:

items.title: 🚀 Features
items.text:
• Attribute Docstring in Quick Documentation — show the string literal that follows a class attribute as its documentation in Quick Documentation popups (PY-63878).
  • Constant should be Final inspection — report module-level constants that should be annotated with Final, with safe quick-fixes that handle aliased module types, from __future__ imports, function-local assignments, wildcard imports, and unknown types.
  • Test/Production editor tabs — keep test and production files in separate editor splits, with a toolbar toggle, configurable split alignment, pytest-config-aware test-file detection, file-color-based tab tinting, and respect for manual tab moves and pinning within a session.

items.title: Documentation Development
items.text: This project uses Zensical with the Material for MkDocs theme to manage its documentation.

items.title: Local Setup
items.text:
To serve and preview the documentation locally, you'll need uv installed.

  1. Serve the documentation (with live-rendered placeholders): 

    scripts/build_docs.py serve

    This wraps zensical serve and starts a local preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000/. The page reloads when you edit anything under docs/ or any feature metadata block under src/main/resources/META-INF/features/*.xml.

    Do not run uv run zensical serve directly

    Our docs use placeholders such as 69, 5, and <!-- feature: <id> --> blocks that are expanded from feature metadata at render time. A plain zensical serve does not invoke that rendering pipeline, so the live preview will show the raw placeholders rather than the production output. Always use the scripts/build_docs.py wrapper.

  2. Build the site once: 

    scripts/build_docs.py build
    Produces site/, matching what the release pipeline builds.

  3. Add a new dependency: 

    uv add <package-name>

items.title: How the docs build works
items.text: The committed files under docs/ are the single source of truth and are never mutated by any build or serve command. Both scripts/build_docs.py build and scripts/build_docs.py serve first render every docs/**/*.md file into a shadow directory at build/docs-rendered-root/docs/ (git-ignored), expanding placeholders and feature blocks, then run zensical against that shadow tree. The committed zensical.toml is likewise copied (nav-trimmed for empty groups) rather than rewritten in place. See scripts/build_docs.py and scripts/docs_ext.py in the repo for details.

items.title: Recovery
items.text:
If git status shows unexpected changes under docs/ — typically left over from an interrupted run of the legacy pre-refactor script — restore them with:

git checkout -- docs/

The current pipeline never writes into docs/, so such leftovers can only come from an older version of the build script or from manual edits.

items.title: Project Structure
items.text:
• zensical.toml: Configuration file for the documentation (theme, navigation, extensions).
  • docs/: Directory containing the Markdown source files for the documentation.
  • docs/index.md: The home page of the documentation.

items.title: Adding an Action to the Code Selection Toolbar
items.text:
PyCharm shows a floating toolbar when text is selected in the editor. To add a BetterPy action to it, register a normal IntelliJ Platform action in the Floating.CodeToolbar action group. The platform then owns selection tracking, positioning, animation, dismissal, scrolling behavior, and accessibility.

Do not create a SelectionListener and position a JBPopup just to reproduce the native selection toolbar.

items.title: Implement the action
items.text:
Use update() to keep the action visible only for a selection in a Python file. Keep this method cheap because the Action System calls it frequently.

package com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.features.example

import com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.ActionUpdateThread
import com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.AnAction
import com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.AnActionEvent
import com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.CommonDataKeys
import com.intellij.openapi.util.TextRange
import com.jetbrains.python.psi.PyFile

class ExampleSelectionAction : AnAction() {
    override fun getActionUpdateThread(): ActionUpdateThread = ActionUpdateThread.BGT

    override fun update(event: AnActionEvent) {
        val editor = event.getData(CommonDataKeys.EDITOR)
        val file = event.getData(CommonDataKeys.PSI_FILE)

        event.presentation.isEnabledAndVisible =
            file is PyFile && editor?.selectionModel?.hasSelection() == true
    }

    override fun actionPerformed(event: AnActionEvent) {
        val project = event.project ?: return
        val editor = event.getData(CommonDataKeys.EDITOR) ?: return
        val file = event.getData(CommonDataKeys.PSI_FILE) as? PyFile ?: return
        val selection = editor.selectionModel
        if (!selection.hasSelection()) return

        val range = TextRange(selection.selectionStart, selection.selectionEnd)
        runFeature(project, editor, file, range)
    }
}

Replace runFeature(...) with the feature's entry point. Also include the feature's settings check in update() so the action disappears when the feature is disabled.

If the action changes a document or PSI:

  • Complete discovery or chooser work before starting the write command.
  • Perform only the final mutation inside WriteCommandAction.
  • Do not resolve PSI or query indexes directly on the EDT.

items.title: Register the action
items.text:
Add the action to the feature's canonical XML under src/main/resources/META-INF/features/:

<actions>
    <action
        id="BetterPy.ExampleSelectionAction"
        class="com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.features.example.ExampleSelectionAction"
        text="Run BetterPy Action"
        description="Runs the action on the selected Python code"
        icon="/icons/exampleSelectionAction.svg">
        <add-to-group group-id="Floating.CodeToolbar" anchor="last"/>
    </action>
</actions>

Use an icon designed for a compact toolbar. Follow the normal BetterPy rules for feature metadata, release-channel registration, settings, recent usage, analytics, and preview filtering when this is a new feature or user-initiated entry point.

items.title: Verify the integration
items.text:
Run PyCharm with the plugin and check that:

  • Selecting text in a .py file shows the action.
  • Clearing the selection hides it.
  • The action stays hidden in non-Python files and when its feature is disabled.
  • Reversed and multi-line selections produce the expected range.
  • Multi-caret selections follow the feature's intended semantics.

If the entire toolbar is missing, check Settings | Advanced Settings | Hide floating toolbar for code editing.

items.title: Related APIs
items.text:
• Floating.CodeToolbar is the native toolbar near selected code and is the correct integration point for an additional action.
  • com.intellij.lang.floatingToolbar configures a language's floating toolbar. Do not use it merely to contribute one Python action.
  • com.intellij.editorFloatingToolbarProvider is for other editor overlay toolbars, often representing persistent editor state.
  • JBPopupFactory is appropriate only when the feature requires a genuinely custom popup rather than the native selection toolbar.

items.title: Faster Local Tests (optional Kover)

./gradlew test -Pkover=false

To enable Kover again, omit -Pkover or pass -Pkover=true.

items.title: Updating Marketplace Screenshots (UI Tests)
items.text:
The documentation and marketplace page rely on automated screenshots generated by UI tests. Since these tests require a running IDE instance via the Robot Server plugin, they are excluded from the standard ./gradlew test task.

To regenerate these screenshots locally:

  1. Start the IDE with the Robot Server: 

    ./gradlew runIdeForUiTests
    Wait for the PyCharm IDE to fully start.

  2. Run the screenshot test class in a separate terminal: 

    ./gradlew test --tests "*PluginPageScreenshotsTest*"

The new screenshots will be saved automatically to docs/assets/marketplace/ and can be committed.

items.title: Updating Feature GIFs (Starter/Driver)
items.text:
New feature recordings should use JetBrains Starter + Driver. The Driver test generates component-scoped PNG frames under build/docs-recordings/<scenario>/, then a small script encodes those frames into a GIF for the docs.

For the Hide overloads Structure View recording:

JAVA_HOME=/Users/jo/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jbr-21.0.10/Contents/Home ./gradlew integrationTest --tests "*HideOverloadsDocsRecordingTest"
scripts/build-docs-gif.sh hide-overloads

The committed output is docs/assets/features/structure-view-overload-hiding/hide-overloads.gif.

items.title: Updating Stable Feature Media
items.text:
Stable feature docs media is tracked in scripts/stable-feature-media.tsv. Each feature in src/main/resources/feature-sets/stable.yaml must appear in that manifest as either:

  • auto: recorded by recording-lab through IDE remote control and encoded as optimized MP4 by scripts/build-docs-mp4-from-video.sh
  • nonvisual: no meaningful user-facing IDE surface for docs media

To regenerate all automated stable feature MP4s:

JAVA_HOME=/Users/jo/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jbr-21.0.10/Contents/Home scripts/build-stable-feature-media.sh

If cropped recordings already exist under build/stable-feature-recordings/stable-feature-docs-features__<feature-id>/, skip the expensive IDE recording step and only re-encode:

scripts/build-stable-feature-media.sh --skip-recordings

The MP4 processing step reads raw.mp4 plus the recording-lab geometry-overlay.json/timeline.jsonl artifacts, derives an ffmpeg crop, and then applies crop, frame-rate reduction, scaling, H.264 encoding, and faststart optimization. Use CROP_MARGIN=<pixels> to tune the default crop padding without re-recording.

For one feature:

scripts/build-stable-feature-media.sh --skip-recordings --feature inherited-attribute-documentation

The manifest is guarded by:

uv run pytest scripts/test_stable_feature_media.py -q

items.title: Pytest Fixture Engine Performance (home-assistant/core)
items.text:
Measure fixture-consumer latency only through a deployed development plugin in an installed PyCharm 261. Do not substitute a Gradle integrationTest, Starter/Driver live test, or a Gradle-launched IDE: those paths do not exercise the deployed IDE process used for this benchmark.

The benchmark corpus is deliberately a shallow sparse checkout containing only tests/. It supplies the fixture declarations and their consumers, but is not a complete or pytest-executable Home Assistant checkout. Reuse a prepared checkout when it contains tests/conftest.py; otherwise create the pinned corpus once:

export BENCHMARK_REF=2026.7.1
export BENCHMARK_REPO="$PWD/build/perf-repos/homeassistant-core-$BENCHMARK_REF"

git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --branch "$BENCHMARK_REF" --sparse \
  https://github.com/home-assistant/core.git "$BENCHMARK_REPO"
git -C "$BENCHMARK_REPO" sparse-checkout set --cone tests
test -f "$BENCHMARK_REPO/tests/conftest.py"

items.title: Deployed PyCharm 261 benchmark
items.text:
Choose one installed build whose displayed Build value begins 261.. The deployment command enables the diagnostic channel only for this benchmark. It also records the exact selected build in build/perf-reports/deploy.log; that value, rather than a guessed 261.* value, is passed to the report.

export BENCHMARK_TOKEN=ha-fixture-perf-secret
export BENCHMARK_REQUESTED_PORT=63342
export DEPLOY_LOG="$PWD/build/perf-reports/deploy.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEPLOY_LOG")"

set -o pipefail
BETTERPY_REQUIRED_PYCHARM_BUILD=261 \
BETTERPY_REMOTE_CONTROL_ENABLED=true \
BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN="$BENCHMARK_TOKEN" \
BETTERPY_IDE_SERVER_PORT="$BENCHMARK_REQUESTED_PORT" \
./scripts/deploy.sh "$BENCHMARK_REPO" | tee "$DEPLOY_LOG"

export IDE_BUILD="$(awk '/^   Build   : 261\./ { print $3; exit }' "$DEPLOY_LOG")"
test -n "$IDE_BUILD"
printf 'Benchmarking deployed PyCharm build: %s\n' "$IDE_BUILD"

After indexing completes, ask the remote-control doctor for the endpoint. The requested server port is only a preference: use the baseUrl that doctor actually returns. The command below writes that result, extracts its discovered base URL, and does not reuse a hard-coded port in the benchmark request.

export DOCTOR_REPORT="$PWD/build/perf-reports/remote-doctor.json"

if ! BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN="$BENCHMARK_TOKEN" \
  python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py \
    --base "http://127.0.0.1:${BENCHMARK_REQUESTED_PORT}/api/betterpy-remote" \
    doctor --try-ports "63340,63341,63342,63343,63344,63345" \
    | tee "$DOCTOR_REPORT"; then
  echo "❌ IDE deployment is not ready." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! BENCHMARK_BASE_URL="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys
report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
if report.get("ready") is not True or not report.get("baseUrl"):
    raise SystemExit("doctor report is not ready")
print(report["baseUrl"])
' "$DOCTOR_REPORT")"; then
  echo "❌ IDE deployment is not ready." >&2
  exit 1
fi
export BENCHMARK_BASE_URL
printf 'Benchmarking doctor-discovered endpoint: %s\n' "$BENCHMARK_BASE_URL"

Run the driver for exactly one fixture in this IDE lifecycle. It verifies /ping, waits for smart mode, measures one process-cold request, performs one unreported warm-up, then records five warm requests. It fails on an empty usage response or a request above the 180-second hang ceiling, and writes JSON with the exact ideBuild, corpus ref, latency samples, and usage count.

python3 scripts/benchmark_homeassistant_fixture.py \
  --repo "$BENCHMARK_REPO" \
  --base-url "$BENCHMARK_BASE_URL" \
  --token "$BENCHMARK_TOKEN" \
  --fixture hass \
  --ide-build "$IDE_BUILD" \
  --ref "$BENCHMARK_REF" \
  --report "$PWD/build/perf-reports/hass.json"

enable_custom_integrations depends on hass; a hass request can warm the same analyzer path. To obtain an independent process-cold report for enable_custom_integrations, deploy/restart the same recorded PyCharm build, repeat the doctor step to set a new BENCHMARK_BASE_URL, then run:

python3 scripts/benchmark_homeassistant_fixture.py \
  --repo "$BENCHMARK_REPO" \
  --base-url "$BENCHMARK_BASE_URL" \
  --token "$BENCHMARK_TOKEN" \
  --fixture enable_custom_integrations \
  --ide-build "$IDE_BUILD" \
  --ref "$BENCHMARK_REF" \
  --report "$PWD/build/perf-reports/enable-custom-integrations.json"

Do not label a second fixture's first request in an already-used IDE process as process-cold. The driver reports end-to-end HTTP latency and usage counts; it does not attribute internal fixture-engine phases.

items.title: Post-benchmark cleanup
items.text:
Disable the temporary diagnostic channel immediately after the final benchmark. Choose the same exact build recorded in IDE_BUILD from the filtered PyCharm menu. This deployment restarts that IDE with remote control disabled and clears the persisted remote-control token; no token or port is supplied to cleanup.

BETTERPY_REQUIRED_PYCHARM_BUILD=261 \
BETTERPY_REMOTE_CONTROL_ENABLED=false \
./scripts/deploy.sh "$BENCHMARK_REPO"

items.title: Import-alias Find Usages Performance (home-assistant/core)
items.text:
Measure import-alias Find Usages through a deployed development plugin in an installed PyCharm 261 and a complete Home Assistant checkout. The sparse tests/ corpus used by the fixture-engine benchmark does not contain the production aliases required by this benchmark.

The pinned workload is Home Assistant 2026.7.1:

export BENCHMARK_REF=2026.7.1
export BENCHMARK_REPO="$PWD/build/perf-repos/homeassistant-core-$BENCHMARK_REF"

git clone --depth 1 --branch "$BENCHMARK_REF" \
  https://github.com/home-assistant/core.git "$BENCHMARK_REPO"
test -f "$BENCHMARK_REPO/homeassistant/core.py"

Deploy the plugin with remote control enabled and discover the actual endpoint using the same Deployed PyCharm 261 benchmark and doctor procedure above. Keep the selected IDE_BUILD, doctor-discovered BENCHMARK_BASE_URL, and token for the following command:

python3 scripts/benchmark_import_alias_find_usages.py \
  --repo "$BENCHMARK_REPO" \
  --base-url "$BENCHMARK_BASE_URL" \
  --token "$BENCHMARK_TOKEN" \
  --ide-build "$IDE_BUILD" \
  --ref "$BENCHMARK_REF" \
  --label "candidate" \
  --report "$PWD/build/perf-reports/import-alias-candidate.json"

The driver waits for smart mode, then runs the default alternating order:

disabled → enabled → enabled → disabled

Every block changes the import-alias-find-usages feature flag, discards one priming request, and records seven paced warm requests. It fails rather than producing a misleading report when a result set changes within or between blocks.

For the pinned corpus and target positions, the default result contract is:

Workload Disabled Enabled Required invariant DOMAIN at homeassistant/core.py:121:1 138 usages 450 usages Disabled locations are a subset of enabled locations; the 312 enabled-only locations contain HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN. BLOCK_LOG_TIMEOUT at homeassistant/core.py:124:1 4 usages 4 usages Location sets are identical.

The DOMAIN workload measures the complete user-visible cost of returning alias-derived locations. The control separates that cost from the always-on feature-gate and no-alias discovery cost. Counts are deliberately overridable for a different pinned corpus with:

--disabled-alias-usage-count
--enabled-alias-usage-count
--enabled-only-alias-usage-count
--control-usage-count

Do not compare means when an IDE pause produces an outlier. The JSON report retains every sample and reports median, mean, minimum, and maximum for each workload/mode. Compare warm medians and first confirm every result-set invariant.

items.title: Candidate-versus-baseline A/B
items.text:
The driver compares the feature enabled and disabled within one deployed build. To compare two plugin implementations, run it for both commits and repeat in the opposite deployment order:

baseline deploy → baseline report
candidate deploy → candidate report
candidate deploy → candidate repeat report
baseline deploy → baseline repeat report

Use the same Home Assistant checkout, installed PyCharm build, JBR, target positions, sample count, and request pacing for every run. Record the commit in --label, for example --label "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)". Do not claim a cross-build speedup unless both implementations preserve the same enabled location set and the repeated medians agree directionally.

items.title: Optional CPU sampling
items.text:
Wall-clock reports answer whether the user waits longer. Capture JFR for the enabled alias block when CPU attribution is needed:

export IDE_PID="$(pgrep -f '/Applications/PyCharm.*\.app/Contents/MacOS/pycharm')"
jcmd "$IDE_PID" JFR.start \
  name=import-alias \
  settings=profile \
  filename="$PWD/build/perf-profiles/import-alias.jfr"

# Run benchmark_import_alias_find_usages.py here.

jcmd "$IDE_PID" JFR.stop name=import-alias
jfr print --events jdk.ExecutionSample \
  "$PWD/build/perf-profiles/import-alias.jfr"

Compare stacks containing PyAliasUsageCollector, KnownSymbols, PSI equivalence, Python resolution, word search, and result deduplication. A JFR profile attributes CPU work but does not replace the response-time and result-location checks in the JSON report.

After every run, apply the remote-control cleanup procedure above. The default driver order ends with the feature disabled, but the temporary remote endpoint and token still require deployment cleanup.

items.title: Web Framework Discovery Diagnostics (home-assistant/core)
items.text:
Measure one direct, all-framework web-application discovery scan through a deployed development plugin in an installed PyCharm 261. This procedure requires the complete Home Assistant source tree: the sparse tests/ corpus above is suitable for the fixture-engine benchmark only and cannot establish web-framework discovery behavior.

items.text: This document explains how features are organized in the BetterPy plugin and how to add a new one.

items.title: Files per feature
items.text:
Each feature consists of XML fragment files only:

  • Canonical feature file: src/main/resources/META-INF/features/<id>.xml — holds plugin registrations and the feature metadata in a dedicated XML comment block.
  • Optional sibling registration files: src/main/resources/META-INF/features/<id>[.<suffix>].xml — additional registrations split by optional dependency or registration type.

Metadata block format inside canonical XML files:

<!-- betterpy-feature
id: add-self-parameter
displayName: Add self parameter
description: Adds a missing self parameter to instance methods
category: CODE_STRUCTURE
maturity: STABLE
defaultEnabled: true
-->

Rules: - Metadata is parsed only from canonical <id>.xml files (not from suffixed siblings). - The metadata id must match the canonical filename <id>.xml. - includeInReadme is optional and defaults to true; set it to false for implementation-detail features that should remain configurable but should not appear in the generated README feature list.

A feature's canonical <id>.xml holds its <extensions>, <actions>, <group>, <extensionPoints>, and <projectListeners> registrations in one place. Sibling files exist only for optional-dependency wiring (.mcp.xml, .yamlsupport.xml, .structuralsearch.xml) and for the Pythonid extension namespace (.pythonid.xml).

At build time, GeneratePluginXmlFragmentsTask globs the committed per-feature XML files, filters them by the active release channel, and emits 4 aggregator files (xi:include indexes). plugin.xml xi:includes the aggregators; the aggregators xi:include the per-feature files. plugin.xml itself only contains plugin metadata, <depends> entries, <resource-bundle>, and the xi:include seam — no <extensions>, <actions>, <group>, or <extensionPoints> live there.

items.title: Filename suffix → aggregator routing
items.text:
The suffix on a per-feature XML filename decides which aggregator references it:

Filename Aggregator Purpose <id>.xml META-INF/plugin-features-index.xml Default target: <extensions> (com.intellij namespace), <actions>, <group>, <extensionPoints>, <projectListeners> <id>.pythonid.xml META-INF/plugin-features-index.xml Pythonid namespace (PythonCore extension points) <id>.mcp.xml META-INF/mcp-support.xml MCP optional dependency (com.intellij.mcpServer) <id>.yamlsupport.xml META-INF/yaml-support.xml YAML optional dependency <id>.structuralsearch.xml META-INF/structural-search.xml Structural Search optional dependency

Each per-feature XML file must declare its own <extensions defaultExtensionNs="…">; the suffix only decides which aggregator xi:includes it, not the namespace wrapping.

items.title: Channel filter
items.text:
src/main/resources/feature-sets/dev.yaml and stable.yaml list the feature ids included in each release channel. Building with -PreleaseChannel=stable (or RELEASE_CHANNEL=stable) filters aggregator entries to the stable list; dev (the default) includes everything.

A feature that is absent from the active channel's set has no xi:include entry in the aggregators, so its extensions are not registered with the platform. The XML file itself is still copied into the build output but nothing loads it.

items.title: The _bootstrap special case
items.text:
src/main/resources/META-INF/features/_bootstrap.xml holds non-user-facing registrations (errorHandler, PluginSettingsState, bootstrap file-based indexes, application configurables, the pytestFixtureProvider extension point, cross-feature action groups like MyPlugin.CopySpecialGroup / PytestExplorerPopupMenu, EmptyAction placeholders, and dev/internal actions). Unlike every other feature, _bootstrap is always emitted regardless of the active channel.

_bootstrap is the only allowed _-prefixed feature id. The generator throws a GradleException if any other feature id starts with _.

items.title: Workflow: adding a new feature
items.text:
1. Create src/main/resources/META-INF/features/<id>.xml and add a <!-- betterpy-feature ... --> metadata block.
  2. Add <idea-plugin><extensions …>…</extensions></idea-plugin> registrations in that canonical file, and create any suffixed variants for optional dependencies / Pythonid registrations.
  3. If the feature should ship in the stable channel, add its id to src/main/resources/feature-sets/stable.yaml.
  4. Run ./gradlew updateReadmeFeatureList if the feature should appear in, or be excluded from, the README feature list.
  5. Run the feature-flag tests to confirm nothing drifted: 
    ./gradlew test --tests com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.featureflags.*

No plugin XML regeneration task is needed — the per-feature XML files are authoritative, and the aggregators are rebuilt automatically during processResources.

items.title: Current state
items.text: Feature declaration metadata is XML-only. Canonical META-INF/features/<id>.xml files are the sole source of feature metadata used by runtime loading, defaults/registry wiring, and build-time plugin XML aggregation.

items.title: Marketplace Release Management
items.text: This guide covers how to manage BetterPy releases on the JetBrains Marketplace using the Marketplace REST API.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• A Marketplace API token (permanent token). Generate one at: https://plugins.jetbrains.com/author/me/tokens
  • The plugin numeric ID. BetterPy's ID is 29896.

Tip: You can look up the numeric ID from the XML plugin ID: 

curl -s "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/plugins?family=intellij&xmlId=com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy" \
  | python3 -m json.tool | grep '"id"'

items.title: Common Operations
items.text:
All examples below use the environment variable $MP_TOKEN for the API token:

export MP_TOKEN="perm:your-token-here"

items.title: List All Published Versions
items.text:
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MP_TOKEN" \
  "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/plugins/29896/updates" \
  | python3 -c "
import json, sys
for u in json.load(sys.stdin):
    ch = u.get('channel') or '(stable)'
    print(f\"id={u['id']}  version={u['version']}  channel={ch}\")
"

Each update has a numeric id (the update ID) which is needed for deletion.

items.title: Delete a Specific Version
items.text:
Use the update ID (not the version string) to delete a release:

curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MP_TOKEN" \
  "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/updates/{updateId}"

Replace {updateId} with the numeric ID from the list command above.

A successful deletion returns HTTP 200 and the message "Update has been removed".

items.title: Delete Multiple Versions
items.text:
To delete several versions at once, first list them to get the update IDs, then loop:

for id in 1234 1235 1236; do
  echo "Deleting update $id..."
  curl -s -w " HTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n" \
    -X DELETE \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $MP_TOKEN" \
    "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/updates/$id"
done

items.title: Upload a New Version
items.text:
Upload to the Stable channel (omit the channel field):

curl -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MP_TOKEN" \
  -F "pluginId=29896" \
  -F "file=@/path/to/plugin.zip" \
  "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/uploadPlugin"

Upload to a pre-release channel (beta, alpha, dev, etc.):

curl -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MP_TOKEN" \
  -F "pluginId=29896" \
  -F "file=@/path/to/plugin.zip" \
  -F "channel=beta" \
  "https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/uploadPlugin"

Important — channel=default is NOT Stable. On the JetBrains Marketplace, the Stable channel is represented by an empty channel value. To publish to Stable, omit the channel form field entirely (or pass an empty string). Passing channel=default creates/uses a custom channel literally named default, which is separate from Stable and will not be shown as the default download.

You can verify via the list endpoint: Stable updates return an empty channel field (""), while custom channels return their literal name.

See VERSIONING.md for channel conventions.

items.title: API Endpoints Reference
items.text:
Operation Method Endpoint Plugin info (by XML ID) GET /api/plugins?family=intellij&xmlId={xmlId} List updates GET /api/plugins/{pluginId}/updates Delete an update DELETE /api/updates/{updateId} Upload plugin POST /plugin/uploadPlugin

Base URL: https://plugins.jetbrains.com

items.title: Important Notes
items.text:
• Deletion is permanent. There is no undo. Always verify the update IDs before deleting.
  • Authentication: All mutating operations require the Authorization: Bearer header with a valid permanent token.
  • Rate limiting: The Marketplace API may rate-limit requests. Add a short delay between bulk operations if needed.
  • The upload endpoint is documented in detail at: Plugin Upload API

items.title: MCP Server Context Passing Guide
items.text: This document explains how to pass and access context (project, editor, caret position) in MCP tools and how to implement navigation.

items.title: Overview
items.text: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server in IntelliJ Platform provides tools that can interact with the IDE. Context is passed through: 1. Automatic context via CoroutineContext 2. Explicit parameters in tool methods

items.title: Accessing the Project
items.text:
The project is the primary context automatically available to MCP tools:

import com.intellij.mcpserver.project
import kotlinx.coroutines.currentCoroutineContext

suspend fun my_tool() {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    // Use project...
}

items.title: Project Context Details
items.text:
• Extension: CoroutineContext.project (throws if no project)
  • Extension: CoroutineContext.projectOrNull (returns null if no project)
  • Source: Defined in McpCallInfo.kt

The project can be specified by: - Environment variables - HTTP headers - Implicit tool parameter projectPath - If only one project is open, it's used automatically

items.title: Example from RefactoringToolset
items.text:
suspend fun rename_refactoring(
    pathInProject: String,
    symbolName: String,
    newName: String,
): String {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(pathInProject)
    // ... rest of implementation
}

items.title: No Automatic Editor Context
items.text: Important: MCP tools do NOT receive automatic editor or caret context. The current editor state is not passed automatically.

items.title: Accessing Open Editors
items.text:
To work with editors, use FileEditorManagerEx:

import com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.ex.FileEditorManagerEx

suspend fun get_open_editors() {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val fileEditorManager = FileEditorManagerEx.getInstanceExAsync(project)

    // Get all open files
    val openFiles = fileEditorManager.openFiles

    // Get active editor
    val activeEditor = fileEditorManager.selectedEditor
    val activeFile = activeEditor?.file
}

items.title: Example from FileToolset
items.text:
@McpTool
suspend fun get_all_open_file_paths(): OpenFilesInfo {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val projectDir = project.projectDirectory

    val fileEditorManager = FileEditorManagerEx.getInstanceExAsync(project)
    val openFiles = fileEditorManager.openFiles
    val filePaths = openFiles.mapNotNull { projectDir.relativizeIfPossible(it) }
    val activeFilePath = fileEditorManager.selectedEditor?.file?.toNioPathOrNull()
        ?.let { projectDir.relativize(it).pathString }

    return OpenFilesInfo(activeFilePath = activeFilePath, openFiles = filePaths)
}

items.title: Design Pattern: Explicit Parameters
items.text:
Caret position is never passed automatically. Tools that need position information must accept explicit parameters:

  • line: Int (1-based line number)
  • column: Int (1-based column number)

items.title: Converting Line/Column to Offset
items.text:
import com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.FileDocumentManager
import com.intellij.psi.PsiDocumentManager
import com.intellij.util.DocumentUtil

suspend fun work_with_position(
    filePath: String,
    line: Int,
    column: Int
) {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $filePath")

    readAction {
        val document = FileDocumentManager.getInstance().getDocument(virtualFile)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot read file: $filePath")

        // Validate line (0-based internally)
        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidLine(line - 1, document)) {
            mcpFail("Line number is out of bounds")
        }

        // Convert to offset
        val lineStartOffset = document.getLineStartOffset(line - 1)
        val offset = lineStartOffset + column - 1

        // Validate offset
        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidOffset(offset, document)) {
            mcpFail("Line and column $line:$column (offset=$offset) is out of bounds")
        }

        // Use offset to find PSI elements
        val psiFile = PsiDocumentManager.getInstance(project).getPsiFile(document)
        val psiReference = psiFile?.findReferenceAt(offset)
        val element = psiReference?.resolve()
    }
}

items.title: Example from CodeInsightToolset
items.text:
@McpTool
suspend fun get_symbol_info(
    @McpDescription("Relative path to file from project root")
    filePath: String,
    @McpDescription("1-based line number")
    line: Int,
    @McpDescription("1-based column number")
    column: Int,
): SymbolInfoResult {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(filePath)
    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().refreshAndFindFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $filePath")

    val (documentationTargets, symbolInfo) = readAction {
        val document = FileDocumentManager.getInstance().getDocument(virtualFile)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot read file: $filePath")
        val psiFile = PsiDocumentManager.getInstance(project).getPsiFile(document)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot get symbol information for file '$filePath'")

        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidLine(line - 1, document)) {
            mcpFail("Line number is out of bounds of the document")
        }

        val lineStartOffset = document.getLineStartOffset(line - 1)
        val offset = lineStartOffset + column - 1

        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidOffset(offset, document)) {
            mcpFail("Line and column $line:$column(offset=$offset) is out of bounds")
        }

        val psiReference = psiFile.findReferenceAt(offset)
        val resolvedReference = psiReference?.resolve()

        documentationTargets(psiFile, offset).map { it.createPointer() } to 
            resolvedReference?.let { getElementSymbolInfo(it, extraLines = 1) }
    }

    // ... rest of implementation
}

items.title: Opening Files in Editor
items.text:
Use FileEditorManagerEx.openFile() to open files:

import com.intellij.openapi.application.EDT
import com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.ex.FileEditorManagerEx
import com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.impl.FileEditorOpenOptions
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

suspend fun open_file(filePath: String) {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(filePath)

    val file = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: LocalFileSystem.getInstance().refreshAndFindFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $filePath")

    // Must be called on EDT (Event Dispatch Thread)
    withContext(Dispatchers.EDT) {
        FileEditorManagerEx.getInstanceExAsync(project)
            .openFile(file, options = FileEditorOpenOptions(requestFocus = true))
    }
}

items.title: Example from FileToolset
items.text:
@McpTool
@McpDescription("""
    Opens the specified file in the JetBrains IDE editor.
    The file path can be absolute or relative to the project root.
""")
suspend fun open_file_in_editor(
    @McpDescription("Relative path to file from project root")
    filePath: String,
) {
    currentCoroutineContext().reportToolActivity(
        McpServerBundle.message("tool.activity.opening.file", filePath)
    )
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(filePath)

    val file = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: LocalFileSystem.getInstance().refreshAndFindFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)

    if (file == null || !file.exists() || !file.isFile) {
        mcpFail("File $filePath doesn't exist or can't be opened")
    }

    withContext(Dispatchers.EDT) {
        FileEditorManagerEx.getInstanceExAsync(project)
            .openFile(file, options = FileEditorOpenOptions(requestFocus = true))
    }
}

items.title: Navigation to Specific Position
items.text:
While not directly exposed in current MCP toolsets, you can navigate to a specific position using OpenFileDescriptor:

import com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.OpenFileDescriptor
import com.intellij.openapi.application.EDT
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

suspend fun navigate_to_position(
    filePath: String,
    line: Int,
    column: Int
) {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $filePath")

    withContext(Dispatchers.EDT) {
        // OpenFileDescriptor uses 0-based line and column
        val descriptor = OpenFileDescriptor(project, virtualFile, line - 1, column - 1)
        descriptor.navigate(true) // true = request focus
    }
}

items.title: 5. Available Context from CoroutineContext
items.text:
From McpCallInfo.kt, the following context is available:

// Project context
val project: Project = currentCoroutineContext().project
val projectOrNull: Project? = currentCoroutineContext().projectOrNull

// Client information
val clientInfo: ClientInfo = currentCoroutineContext().clientInfo
// Contains: name, version

// Tool descriptor
val toolDescriptor: McpToolDescriptor = currentCoroutineContext().currentToolDescriptor

// Full call info
val callInfo: McpCallInfo = currentCoroutineContext().mcpCallInfo
// Contains: callId, clientInfo, project, mcpToolDescriptor, rawArguments, meta, 
//           mcpSessionOptions, headers

items.title: Pattern 1: File-based Tool
items.text:
@McpTool
suspend fun my_file_tool(
    @McpDescription("Relative path to file from project root")
    pathInProject: String
): String {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(pathInProject)

    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: LocalFileSystem.getInstance().refreshAndFindFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $pathInProject")

    return readAction {
        val document = FileDocumentManager.getInstance().getDocument(virtualFile)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot read file: $pathInProject")

        val psiFile = PsiDocumentManager.getInstance(project).getPsiFile(document)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot get PSI file: $pathInProject")

        // Work with psiFile...
        "Success"
    }
}

items.title: Pattern 2: Position-based Tool
items.text:
@McpTool
suspend fun my_position_tool(
    @McpDescription("Relative path to file from project root")
    pathInProject: String,
    @McpDescription("1-based line number")
    line: Int,
    @McpDescription("1-based column number")
    column: Int
): String {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(pathInProject)

    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $pathInProject")

    return readAction {
        val document = FileDocumentManager.getInstance().getDocument(virtualFile)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot read file: $pathInProject")

        val psiFile = PsiDocumentManager.getInstance(project).getPsiFile(document)
            ?: mcpFail("Cannot get PSI file: $pathInProject")

        // Validate and convert to offset
        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidLine(line - 1, document)) {
            mcpFail("Line number is out of bounds")
        }

        val lineStartOffset = document.getLineStartOffset(line - 1)
        val offset = lineStartOffset + column - 1

        if (!DocumentUtil.isValidOffset(offset, document)) {
            mcpFail("Position $line:$column is out of bounds")
        }

        // Work with offset...
        val element = psiFile.findElementAt(offset)
        "Success"
    }
}

items.title: Pattern 3: Editor Manipulation Tool
items.text:
@McpTool
suspend fun my_editor_tool(
    @McpDescription("Relative path to file from project root")
    pathInProject: String
): String {
    val project = currentCoroutineContext().project
    val resolvedPath = project.resolveInProject(pathInProject)

    val virtualFile = LocalFileSystem.getInstance().findFileByNioFile(resolvedPath)
        ?: mcpFail("File not found: $pathInProject")

    // Open file in editor
    withContext(Dispatchers.EDT) {
        FileEditorManagerEx.getInstanceExAsync(project)
            .openFile(virtualFile, options = FileEditorOpenOptions(requestFocus = true))
    }

    return "File opened successfully"
}

items.title: 7. Key Takeaways
items.text:
1. Project context is automatically available via currentCoroutineContext().project
  2. Editor context is NOT automatic - use FileEditorManagerEx to access editors
  3. Caret position is NOT automatic - accept line and column as explicit parameters
  4. Navigation is done via FileEditorManagerEx.openFile() or OpenFileDescriptor.navigate()
  5. File paths should be relative to project root and passed as parameters
  6. Position parameters should be 1-based (line and column) for user-friendliness
  7. Offset calculations are 0-based internally (convert from 1-based parameters)
  8. EDT thread is required for UI operations like opening files
  9. Read actions are required for PSI operations
  10. Write actions are required for modifying files

items.title: Settings
items.text: The Python BetterPy plugin is highly configurable. You can find its settings under: Settings/Preferences > Languages & Frameworks > Python BetterPy.

items.title: Feature Toggles
items.text: Almost every intention, inspection, and action can be enabled or disabled individually. This allows you to tailor the plugin to your specific workflow and avoid clutter if you don't use certain features.

items.title: Type Wrapping Settings
items.text:
• Prefer project types: When wrapping a value that could match multiple types (e.g., in a Union), should the plugin prioritize types defined in your project over standard library types?
  • Include stdlib types: Should standard library types (like Path) be suggested as wrapping candidates?

items.title: Parameter Object Settings
items.text:
• Default base type: Choose the default class type used when creating a new Parameter Object. Options typically include:
    • dataclass (Default)
    • pydantic.BaseModel
    • NamedTuple
    • TypedDict

items.title: Import Settings
items.text: • Use relative imports: Toggle the preference for relative imports when the plugin generates new code or performs refactorings.

items.title: Actions
items.text: Beyond intentions and inspections, the plugin provides several global and context-specific actions.

items.title: Copy Special Menu
items.text:
Found under Edit > Copy Special or in context menus.

  • BetterPy: Copy with Dependencies: Copies selected code along with its local dependencies and imports.
  • Copy Package Content: Copies the content of an entire Python package.
  • Copy Build Number: Copies the current IDE build number (useful for bug reports).
  • Copy Fully Qualified Names (FQN): Copies the full import path of the selected symbol(s).

items.title: Pytest Tree Actions
items.text:
Available when right-clicking nodes in the Pytest results tool window.

  • Copy Pytest Node IDs: Useful for running specific tests from the command line.
  • Copy Stacktrace: Provides a cleaned-up version of the failure stacktrace.
  • Toggle Pytest Skip: Skips or unskips the selected test(s).

items.title: Navigation Actions
items.text: • Jump to Pytest Node: Navigates from a test function in the editor to its result in the test tree.

items.title: Console & Usage Filtering
items.text: Tools to reduce noise and improve focus during development and debugging.

items.title: Console Filter
items.text: The Py Message Console Filter automatically processes output in the Python console and execution tool windows. It can highlight or hide specific patterns, making it easier to spot relevant information in verbose logs.

items.title: Usage Filtering Rules
items.text: The plugin introduces custom rules for the Find Usages (⌥F7 / Alt+F7) functionality.

items.title: Type Annotation Usage Filtering
items.text: Allows you to filter out usages that only occur within type annotations. This is extremely useful when you want to find where a class is actually instantiated or called, rather than just where its name is used as a type hint.

items.title: Import Handling
items.text: The plugin provides advanced features for managing Python imports, especially useful in large DDD projects with complex folder structures.

items.title: Relative vs Absolute Imports
items.text: The plugin can be configured to prefer relative imports when moving code or performing refactorings within the same package.

items.title: Restore Source Root Prefix
items.text: When copying FQNs or performing refactorings, the plugin can automatically handle source root prefixes to ensure that imports remain valid regardless of how your IDE is configured (e.g., whether the src folder is marked as a source root).

items.title: Export Symbol to Target
items.text: This feature helps you move a symbol and update its imports, or "export" it through a public API module (like __init__.py).

items.title: File-Based vs Stub-Based Indices in IntelliJ Platform
items.text: This document explains the two main indexing mechanisms available in the IntelliJ Platform, and why PyLambdaFileIndex correctly uses a file-based index rather than a stub-based one.

items.title: File-Based Indices (FileBasedIndexExtension)
items.text:
A file-based index operates directly on raw file content. The platform feeds each file's bytes (and optionally its PSI tree) to a DataIndexer, which produces a map of keys → values. The index is stored on disk and queried via FileBasedIndex.getInstance().

Key characteristics:

  • Input: raw FileContent (bytes + lazily-built PSI). The indexer receives a FileContent object and can call inputData.psiFile to get the PSI tree.
  • Scope: any file type — source files, library JARs, .class files, .xml, etc.
  • Query API: FileBasedIndex.getContainingFiles(name, key, scope), getValues(...), getAllKeys(...).
  • Rebuild trigger: the file's content changes (timestamp/hash).
  • Base class: ScalarIndexExtension<K> (keys only, no values) or FileBasedIndexExtension<K, V>.

items.title: Stub-Based Indices (StubIndexExtension)
items.text:
A stub index operates on the stub tree — a lightweight, serialisable skeleton of the PSI tree that captures only the declarations (classes, functions, fields, top-level assignments, etc.) without method bodies or expressions.

Key characteristics:

  • Input: a StubElement tree produced by the language's IStubFileElementType / StubElementType. The stub tree is built once and cached separately from the full PSI.
  • Scope: only files whose language has a stub-producing element type. For Python this means .py files processed by PyFileElementType.
  • Query API: StubIndex.getInstance().get(key, name, project, scope) — returns PSI elements directly (e.g. PyFunction, PyClass).
  • Rebuild trigger: the stub tree changes (i.e. the file's declarations change).
  • Base class: StringStubIndexExtension<Psi> or StubIndexExtension<K, Psi>.
  • Populated via: indexStub(stub, sink) on a StubElementType, or via a CustomTargetExpressionStubType extension point (see fixture-stub-index.md).

items.title: When to Use Each
items.text:
Criterion File-Based Index Stub-Based Index What you need to find Files (or arbitrary data) Named declarations (classes, functions, …) Data lives in Expressions, bodies, any syntax Top-level / class-level declarations only Language requirement Any file type Language must produce stubs Query returns VirtualFile or raw values PSI elements Typical use case "Which files contain X?" "Give me the PyFunction named foo"

Rule of thumb: use a stub index when you are indexing named declarations that appear in the stub tree. Use a file-based index when you need to record a fact about a file as a whole, or when the data you care about lives inside expressions or function bodies (which are not part of the stub tree).

items.title: Why PyLambdaFileIndex Must Be File-Based
items.text:
PyLambdaFileIndex (in core/index/PyLambdaFileIndex.kt) answers the question:

"Which Python source files contain at least one lambda expression?"

There are two concrete reasons why a stub-based index cannot answer this question.

items.title: 1. Lambda expressions are not part of the stub tree
items.text:
The Python stub tree captures declarations: PyFunction, PyClass, PyTargetExpression at module/class scope, etc. A PyLambdaExpression is an expression — it can appear inside a function body, a default argument, a list comprehension, or any other expression context. Expression nodes are deliberately excluded from stubs to keep them small and fast.

Because PyLambdaExpression nodes are never present in the stub tree, a StubElementType for them cannot be registered, and indexStub() would never be called for them. A stub index simply has no access to this data.

items.title: 2. The index records a file-level fact, not a named declaration
items.text:
PyLambdaFileIndex stores a single marker key ("lambda") per file — it is a boolean "this file has lambdas" flag. Stub indices are designed to map names to PSI elements (e.g. function name → PyFunction). There is no named declaration to return here; the caller only needs the VirtualFile to open it and inspect it further.

The query call in the companion object reflects this exactly:

// PyLambdaFileIndex.kt
fun findFilesWithLambdas(project: Project, scope: GlobalSearchScope): Collection<VirtualFile> {
    return FileBasedIndex.getInstance().getContainingFiles(NAME, LAMBDA_MARKER, scope)
}

getContainingFiles is a FileBasedIndex API — there is no equivalent on StubIndex because stub queries return PSI elements, not files.

items.title: 3. The indexer uses the full PSI tree
items.text:
The indexer calls PsiTreeUtil.findChildOfType(psiFile, PyLambdaExpression::class.java), which walks the complete PSI tree including all expression nodes. This is only possible in a DataIndexer that receives a FileContent object with a lazily-built full PSI tree. A stub-based indexer only ever sees the stub tree, which, as noted above, contains no PyLambdaExpression nodes.

// PyLambdaFileIndex.kt — indexer body
override fun getIndexer(): DataIndexer<String, Void, FileContent> {
    return DataIndexer { inputData ->
        val result = mutableMapOf<String, Void?>()
        if (inputData.fileType == PythonFileType.INSTANCE) {
            val psiFile = inputData.psiFile as? PyFile ?: return@DataIndexer result
            // PsiTreeUtil walks the FULL PSI tree — not available in stub indexers
            val hasLambda = PsiTreeUtil.findChildOfType(psiFile, PyLambdaExpression::class.java) != null
            if (hasLambda) result[LAMBDA_MARKER] = null
        }
        result
    }
}

items.title: Contrast: When a Stub Index Would Be Correct
items.text:
For comparison, consider fixture-stub-index.md, which describes indexing assigned fixtures of the form x = pytest.fixture()(func). That case is a good fit for a stub index because:

  • The indexed node is a PyTargetExpression — a top-level assignment, which is part of the stub tree.
  • The query returns a named PSI element (PyTargetExpression for fixture name x).
  • The CustomTargetExpressionStubType extension point already hooks into stub building for exactly this pattern.

PyLambdaFileIndex is the opposite: the data lives in expressions (not declarations), the result is a file (not a PSI element), and the detection requires a full-PSI walk. A file-based index is therefore not just acceptable — it is the only correct choice.
