items.title: Refactoring & Code Transformations
items.text: BetterPy provides 8 refactoring intentions and actions — from populating function arguments to extracting protocols and converting between code patterns.

items.title: Make parameter optional
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating

Convert a required function parameter into an optional parameter without manually editing the signature. BetterPy adds a default value at the declaration site and leaves the rest of the signature intact.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on a required parameter and use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "BetterPy: Make optional".

items.title: Example
items.text:
def greet(name: str, title: str):
    return f"{title} {name}"

becomes:

def greet(name: str, title: str = ""):
    return f"{title} {name}"

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Function and method parameters that currently have no default value.
  • Typed and untyped parameters.
  • Parameters in regular Python source files in your project.
  • Existing annotations and surrounding formatting.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Parameters that already have a default value.
  • Parameters whose position cannot accept a default without changing Python's required-parameter ordering rules.
  • *args, **kwargs, and synthetic parameters.
  • Files outside your own project sources.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The inserted default is intentionally conservative. Review it after applying the intention when the domain needs a different sentinel or value.
  • The feature is gated by the Make parameter optional setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Arguments.

items.title: Make parameter mandatory
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating

Convert an optional function parameter back into a required parameter. BetterPy removes the default value from the signature so callers must provide an argument explicitly.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on an optional parameter and use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "BetterPy: Make mandatory".

items.title: Example
items.text:
def greet(name: str, title: str = ""):
    return f"{title} {name}"

becomes:

def greet(name: str, title: str):
    return f"{title} {name}"

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Function and method parameters with simple default values.
  • Typed and untyped parameters.
  • Regular project Python files.
  • Keeping annotations, decorators, and the surrounding function body unchanged.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Parameters without a default value.
  • *args, **kwargs, and generated parameters.
  • Changes to call sites. After applying the intention, inspect callers and update any that relied on the removed default.
  • Files outside your own project sources.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• This is a signature-editing intention, not a full call-site migration.
  • The feature is gated by the Make parameter mandatory setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Arguments.

items.title: Top-level extract function
items.text:
Since 2026.06.0 · Maturity Incubating · Issues PY-40840PY-44636PY-73852

Extracts selected module-level Python statements into a new function while keeping the code explicit about inputs and outputs.

items.title: Before
items.text:
raw_total = subtotal + tax
discounted_total = raw_total - discount
print(discounted_total)

items.title: After
items.text:
def calculate_discounted_total(subtotal, tax, discount):
    raw_total = subtotal + tax
    discounted_total = raw_total - discount
    return discounted_total


discounted_total = calculate_discounted_total(subtotal, tax, discount)
print(discounted_total)

The action is available through PyCharm's extract method refactoring when the current selection is at module level and can be represented as a standalone function.

items.title: Parameter object refactoring
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating · Issues PY-59270

Introduce Parameter Object turns a long parameter list into a single object parameter. Inline Parameter Object performs the reverse transformation when the object no longer carries enough value to stay separate.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text:
• Place the caret inside a function and use Refactor | BetterPy: Introduce Parameter Object....
  • Place the caret on a function that takes an inlineable parameter object and use Refactor | BetterPy: Inline Parameter Object....
  • When the gutter feature is enabled, a parameter-object gutter icon can start the introduce flow on eligible functions.

items.title: Introduce example
items.text:
def create_order(customer_id: int, product_id: str, quantity: int, urgent: bool):
    ...

can become:

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class CreateOrderParams:
    customer_id: int
    product_id: str
    quantity: int
    urgent: bool


def create_order(params: CreateOrderParams):
    ...

Call sites are rewritten to construct the parameter object:

create_order(CreateOrderParams(customer_id, product_id, quantity, urgent))

items.title: Inline example
items.text:
@dataclass
class SearchParams:
    query: str
    limit: int


def search(params: SearchParams):
    return client.search(params.query, params.limit)

can become:

def search(query: str, limit: int):
    return client.search(query, limit)

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Dataclass-backed parameter objects by default.
  • Alternate parameter-object base types configured in Settings | BetterPy | Parameter Object Refactoring.
  • Rewriting function bodies and known call sites.
  • Preserving type annotations when the source signature contains them.
  • Inline refactoring for simple object-field access patterns.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Functions whose parameters or usages cannot be rewritten predictably.
  • Highly dynamic call sites where argument mapping is ambiguous.
  • Parameter objects that are not recognized as a supported shape.
  • Blindly deleting object classes when usages remain outside the refactoring scope.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The feature is incubating. Preview the refactoring and review the changed files before committing the result.
  • The feature is gated by the Parameter object refactoring setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Parameter Object.

items.title: Parameter object MCP tool
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Stable

The Parameter object MCP tool exposes BetterPy's parameter-object refactoring flow to MCP-capable assistants. It lets an assistant request the same IDE-backed transformation instead of trying to rewrite Python source text on its own.

items.title: How to use
items.text: Connect an MCP client to the IDE, then ask it to introduce or inline a parameter object for a specific function. The tool runs inside the IDE context, so it can use project PSI, inspections, and refactoring infrastructure.

items.title: Example request
items.text:
Introduce a parameter object for create_order in orders/service.py.
Use a dataclass and update call sites.

The assistant can route that request to BetterPy's MCP tool. The IDE performs the refactoring and returns the result through the MCP session.

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Assistant-triggered introduce parameter object operations.
  • The same target validation used by the interactive refactoring.
  • Project-aware source edits rather than standalone text replacement.
  • Respecting the parameter-object feature settings configured in the IDE.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Running when the Parameter object refactoring feature is disabled.
  • Applying transformations to unsupported or ambiguous function signatures.
  • Replacing human review. You should still inspect the produced diff.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• This feature is useful when you want an assistant to orchestrate refactoring while the IDE remains responsible for correctness-sensitive edits.
  • The feature is gated by the Parameter object MCP tool setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Parameter Object.

items.title: Change visibility
items.text:
Since 2026.04.13 · Maturity Stable

Toggle a Python symbol between public and private naming without manually renaming the declaration and every call site. BetterPy reuses the IntelliJ rename refactoring, so all references in the project are updated together with the declaration.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on the name of a function, class, or top-level/class-level variable, then ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter → "Change visibility: make private" or "Change visibility: make public". The intention text adapts to the current name: - A name without a leading underscore offers "make private" and renames name → _name. - A name starting with _ offers "make public" and strips leading underscores (_name → name, __name → name).

items.title: Example
items.text:
Make privateMake public 

def calculate(value):
    return value * 2

print(calculate(2))
becomes: 
def _calculate(value):
    return value * 2

print(_calculate(2))


class _Helper:
    pass

def build() -> _Helper:
    return _Helper()
becomes: 
class Helper:
    pass

def build() -> Helper:
    return Helper()

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Functions, classes, and assignment targets (module-level and class-level attributes).
  • Updates every reference in the project via the standard rename refactoring, so imports and qualified usages stay in sync.
  • Works on names with one or more leading underscores; making a name public removes all of them.
  • When invoked on a method that is also defined in a super class or overridden in subclasses, BetterPy asks before changing the rest of the hierarchy. The dialog lists the affected super classes and subclasses and lets you choose between "Rename in Hierarchy", "Rename Only This Method", or "Cancel".

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Dunder names such as __init__ or __call__ — these have language-defined semantics.
  • Pytest test functions (test_*) and test classes (Test*), since renaming them would hide them from collection.
  • Symbols defined in conftest.py, where the _ prefix would change pytest fixture discovery.
  • Names whose target form would collide with a Python reserved keyword.
  • Files outside your own project (library or stub sources).

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The intention is gated by the Change visibility setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Code Transformations and is enabled by default.
  • Because the rename runs through RenameProcessor, conflicts (for example an existing symbol with the target name) are surfaced through the standard refactoring conflict dialog rather than silently overwriting code.

items.title: Dict access conversion
items.text:
Since 2026.04.13 · Maturity Incubating · Issues PY-54845

This feature bundles three related intentions that help you switch between the most common dictionary lookup styles depending on whether you want terse code, explicit fallback handling, or exception-driven control flow.

All three intentions only activate for expressions BetterPy can verify as mappings. That keeps the feature from appearing on unrelated subscription syntax such as lists, tuples, or arbitrary objects that just happen to define a get() method.

items.title: Convert bracket access to .get()
items.text:
How to invoke: ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter on mapping[key] → "BetterPy: Replace 'dict[key]' with 'dict.get(key)'"

Use this when a missing key should quietly yield None instead of raising KeyError.

timeout = config["timeout"]

becomes:

timeout = config.get("timeout")

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Ordinary dictionary and mapping lookups such as payload["id"].
  • Variable keys like payload[key_name].
  • Tuple keys, including the comma form mapping[a, b], which is rewritten to mapping.get((a, b)).
  • Complex mapping expressions such as factory().cache["users"].
  • Inline comments and spacing inside the brackets; BetterPy preserves the bracket contents instead of rebuilding them from scratch.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Assignment targets like mapping[key] = value.
  • Deletions such as del mapping[key].
  • Augmented assignments like mapping[key] += 1.
  • Non-mapping operands such as lists.

Those cases are skipped because .get() changes the meaning: it reads a value, but it cannot stand in for write/delete syntax.

items.title: Convert .get() to bracket access
items.text:
How to invoke: ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter on mapping.get(key) → "BetterPy: Replace 'dict.get(key)' with 'dict[key]'"

Use this when a key is expected to exist and surfacing KeyError is preferable to silently returning None.

username = payload.get("username")

becomes:

username = payload["username"]

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• One-argument .get() calls.
  • Positional keys such as mapping.get(key).
  • Keyword style calls like mapping.get(key=name), which become mapping[name].

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• .get() calls with a default, for example mapping.get("timeout", 30).
  • Calls with zero arguments or more than one effective argument.
  • Calls on non-mapping values.
  • Shadowed or unrelated get call sites where BetterPy cannot prove the qualifier is a mapping lookup.

This restriction matters because mapping.get(key, default) is not equivalent to mapping[key]; replacing it would drop the fallback value.

items.title: Convert .get(..., default) to try / except KeyError
items.text:
How to invoke: ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter on mapping.get(key, default) used as a full assignment or return value → "BetterPy: Replace 'dict.get(key, default)' with try/except KeyError"

Use this when you want explicit exception-based control flow while keeping the same fallback result.

result = payload.get("name", "unknown")

becomes:

try:
    result = payload["name"]
except KeyError:
    result = "unknown"

It also works for direct returns:

return payload.get("name", "unknown")

becomes:

try:
    return payload["name"]
except KeyError:
    return "unknown"

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Full assignment statements with exactly one target.
  • Full return statements.
  • Positional and keyword forms for key and default.
  • Safe default expressions such as literals, constants, references, and simple constant-style subscriptions.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Nested or partial expressions like foo(payload.get("name", "unknown")).
  • Assignments with multiple targets.
  • Calls without a default value.
  • Defaults that may have side effects or are expensive to duplicate.

The generated try block repeats the lookup once and the fallback once, so BetterPy only offers the intention when that duplication is predictable and safe.

items.title: Convert try / except KeyError to .get()
items.text:
How to invoke: ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter inside a qualifying try block → "BetterPy: Replace try-except with dict.get"

Use this when explicit exception handling is unnecessary and a compact lookup reads better.

try:
    result = payload["name"]
except KeyError:
    result = "unknown"

becomes:

result = payload.get("name", "unknown")

It also supports the common initialization-plus-pass pattern:

result = "unknown"
try:
    result = payload["name"]
except KeyError:
    pass

becomes:

result = payload.get("name", "unknown")

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• A single except KeyError clause.
  • A try block containing exactly one statement.
  • Assignment or return forms.
  • Fallbacks expressed as a literal or simple reference.
  • Tuple keys and parenthesized complex mapping expressions.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• try statements with else or finally blocks.
  • Multiple except clauses.
  • Nested subscriptions such as mapping[a][b], where .get() would not preserve the same failure boundary.
  • Complex fallback expressions.

These constraints ensure the shorter .get() form stays semantically equivalent to the original exception-handling code.

items.title: When to prefer each form
items.text:
• Use mapping[key] when the key is required and a missing value should fail loudly.
  • Use mapping.get(key) when absence is expected and None is a meaningful signal.
  • Use mapping.get(key, default) when you want a compact fallback.
  • Use try / except KeyError when the fallback path needs to be visually explicit or is about to grow into more than a single expression.

Because BetterPy supports moving in both directions, you can start with the clearest form for the current situation and change it later without rewriting the statement by hand.

items.title: Toggle enum member value
items.text:
Since 2026.05.2 · Maturity Stable

Toggle an enum member reference between the enum member object and its literal value. This is useful when a call site or assertion needs to switch between comparing enum members and comparing their serialized values.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on an enum member reference or on a literal value with an expected enum type, then use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "BetterPy: Toggle enum member / value".

items.title: Example
items.text:
from enum import Enum


class Color(Enum):
    RED = "red"


payload = Color.RED

becomes:

payload = "red"

Running the intention on "red" changes it back to Color.RED when the expression has an expected Color type, such as an annotated assignment or annotated function parameter.

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Members of Enum, IntEnum, StrEnum, Flag, and IntFlag classes.
  • Qualified enum member references such as Color.RED.
  • Literal values whose expected type resolves to an enum class.
  • Enum references used inside expressions, assignments, and comparisons.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Bare names such as RED where the enum class is not part of the reference.
  • Literal values without an expected enum type annotation.
  • Attributes on non-enum classes.
  • Longer attribute chains such as Color.RED.name or Color.RED.custom.
  • Files outside your own project sources.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The intention changes call-site references only. It does not rewrite enum member declarations.
  • The feature is gated by the Toggle enum member value setting under Settings | BetterPy | Refactoring & code transformations | Type Editing.

items.title: Typing & Type Hints
items.text: BetterPy enhances PyCharm's type system support with smart wrapping/unwrapping intentions, completions driven by expected types, and convenient annotation editing tools.

items.title: NewType/TypeVar/ParamSpec reference & rename
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Stable · Issues PY-82966PY-53658

Python typing helpers often repeat a symbol name inside a string literal. BetterPy connects those string literals to the Python symbol so navigation and rename stay consistent.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text:
• Use ⌘+Click / Ctrl+Click on the name string in NewType, TypeVar, or ParamSpec calls to jump to the matching assigned symbol, for example from "UserId" to UserId.
  • Use ⇧F6 / Shift+F6 on the Python symbol to rename it. BetterPy keeps the matching string literal in sync.
  • For NewType, if the string was edited manually and no longer matches the assigned symbol, use the quick-fix on the highlighted string to update it.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
NewTypeTypeVarParamSpec 
from typing import NewType

UserId = NewType("UserId", int)

from typing import TypeVar

ItemT = TypeVar("ItemT")

from typing import ParamSpec

P = ParamSpec("P")

Renaming UserId to AccountId updates both the target name and the string literal:

AccountId = NewType("AccountId", int)

If a NewType literal drifted manually, BetterPy highlights the mismatch and offers to update the string:

AccountId = NewType("UserId", int)

The quick-fix rewrites it to:

AccountId = NewType("AccountId", int)

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• typing.NewType, typing.TypeVar, and typing.ParamSpec style declarations.
  • String-literal references from the helper call back to the assigned Python symbol.
  • Rename synchronization for the declaration and the literal.
  • A quick-fix for manual NewType string drift when the literal no longer matches the assigned symbol. PyCharm's built-in quick-fix handles the same drift for TypeVar and ParamSpec.
  • Navigation and reference search in regular project files.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Calls where the string literal intentionally does not match the assigned symbol.
  • Dynamic names or computed string arguments.
  • Unrelated string literals that happen to contain the same text.
  • Library and stub files outside your project.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• This feature reduces rename drift in typing-heavy modules without changing runtime behavior.
  • The feature is gated by the NewType/TypeVar/ParamSpec reference & rename setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Completions.

items.title: Strip signature type annotations
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Stable

Remove all type annotations from a function signature in one action. The function body stays unchanged, making this a focused cleanup tool for examples, dynamic APIs, or code that should not expose annotations.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret inside a typed function signature and use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "Strip type annotations from signature".

items.title: Example
items.text:
def create_user(name: str, email: str, age: int) -> User:
    ...

becomes:

def create_user(name, email, age):
    ...

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Parameter annotations.
  • Return annotations.
  • Regular functions and methods.
  • Preserving default values, decorators, parameter order, and the function body.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Removing annotations outside the current function signature.
  • Rewriting variable annotations in the body.
  • Changing call sites.
  • Files outside your own project sources.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• This action is intentionally narrow: it removes signature annotations only.
  • The feature is gated by the Strip signature type annotations setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Type Editing.

items.title: Copy method annotations from parent
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating

Copy missing type annotations from a parent method into an overriding method. This is useful when subclass methods intentionally keep the same signature but were written without annotations.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on an overriding method and use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "Copy type annotations from parent".

items.title: Example
items.text:
class Handler:
    def handle(self, event: Event) -> Result:
        ...


class AuditHandler(Handler):
    def handle(self, event):
        ...

becomes:

class AuditHandler(Handler):
    def handle(self, event: Event) -> Result:
        ...

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Copying missing parameter annotations.
  • Copying missing return annotations.
  • Keeping existing child annotations when they are already present.
  • Adding imports required by copied annotation names.
  • Rewriting common alias imports so the resulting annotation resolves in the child file.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Methods with no typed parent method.
  • Signature shapes that do not line up with the parent method.
  • Blindly overwriting annotations already present on the child.
  • Applying a fix when import or name conflicts need explicit review.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The intention can be used directly, and the overridden-method inspection can offer it as a quick-fix.
  • The feature is gated by the Copy method annotations from parent setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Type Editing.

items.title: Missing |None annotation inspection
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating · Issues PY-88504

PyCharm 2026.1 and newer also reports parameters whose default value is None but whose type annotation does not admit None. BetterPy keeps its own inspection for the same code shape so the "BetterPy: Add | None to annotation" quick-fix is available as an inspection quick-fix in the highlighted-code actions.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Place the caret on the highlighted None default or initializer, then use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "BetterPy: Add | None to annotation".

items.title: Example
items.text:
def fetch_user(user_id: str, timeout: int = None):
    ...

becomes:

def fetch_user(user_id: str, timeout: int | None = None):
    ...

It also handles annotated assignments with None initializers:

current_user: User = None

becomes:

current_user: User | None = None

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Parameters with None defaults.
  • Annotated assignments initialized with None.
  • Existing union syntax such as Union[T, None] and T | None.
  • Quick-fixing only the annotation while preserving the default expression.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Values that are not actually initialized with None.
  • Unannotated parameters or assignments.
  • Annotations that already allow None.
  • Library and stub files outside your project.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• PyCharm 2026.1 and newer has its own diagnostic for this pattern. BetterPy's inspection intentionally overlaps with it so the BetterPy quick-fix appears with the highlighted inspection actions.
  • The quick-fix is gated by the Missing |None annotation inspection setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Code Inspections.

items.title: Overridden method missing type annotations inspection
items.text:
Since 2026.04.05 · Maturity Incubating

Report overriding methods that dropped type annotations from the parent method. The quick-fix copies the missing annotations from the parent so subclass signatures stay readable and type-checker friendly.

items.title: How to invoke
items.text: Enable the inspection, place the caret on a highlighted override, then use ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter -> "Copy type annotations from parent".

items.title: Example
items.text:
class Repository:
    def save(self, item: Order) -> None:
        ...


class SqlRepository(Repository):
    def save(self, item):
        ...

becomes:

class SqlRepository(Repository):
    def save(self, item: Order) -> None:
        ...

items.title: What it supports
items.text:
• Overrides that inherit parameter and return annotations from a parent method.
  • Partial fixes when only some annotations are missing.
  • Import insertion when copied annotations need names from another module.
  • Alias-aware imports in common cases.

items.title: What it deliberately avoids
items.text:
• Methods that do not override a typed parent method.
  • Overrides where the parent and child signatures are incompatible.
  • Applying a fix when copied names would introduce unresolved or conflicting references without user confirmation.
  • Library and stub files outside your project.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• This inspection is the diagnostic companion to the Copy method annotations from parent intention.
  • The feature is gated by the Overridden method missing type annotations inspection setting under Settings | BetterPy | Typing & Type Hints | Code Inspections.

items.title: Install from JetBrains Marketplace
items.text:
1. Open Settings → Plugins → Marketplace.
  2. Search for BetterPy.
  3. Click Install and restart the IDE when prompted.

items.title: Install from Disk
items.text:
1. Download the latest .zip from the GitHub Releases page.
  2. Open Settings → Plugins → → Install Plugin from Disk…
  3. Select the downloaded .zip file and restart the IDE.

items.title: First-Use Orientation
items.text: After installation, BetterPy is ready to go with sensible defaults.

items.title: Status Bar Widget
items.text: Look for the BetterPy widget in the bottom status bar. It shows the plugin status and provides quick access to settings.

items.title: Settings Panel
items.text:
Open Settings → Tools → BetterPy to see all feature toggles organized by group:

  • Typing & Type Hints
  • Refactoring & Code Transformations
  • Testing (Pytest)
  • Imports & Module Boundaries
  • Navigation & Discovery
  • Code Quality & Safety
  • Productivity Actions
  • IDE Customization

Each feature can be individually enabled or disabled. Incubating features are marked with .

items.title: Your First Intention: Make Parameter Optional
items.text:
Try BetterPy right away with the Make Parameter Optional intention:

BeforeAfter 
def create_user(name: str, email: str, age: int):
    pass
# Place caret on `age` parameter

def create_user(name: str, email: str, age: int | None = None):
    pass

How to invoke: Place the caret on a required parameter and press ⌥⏎ / Alt+Enter, then select "BetterPy: Make optional".

Tip

Make Parameter Optional adds a default value to the selected parameter. Use the complementary Make Parameter Mandatory intention to remove a default value.

items.title: Inspections
items.text: The plugin provides several inspections to ensure code quality and adherence to DDD principles.

items.title: Missing Dataclass Decorator
items.text: Warns when a class appears to be used as a Value Object (e.g., it's a subclass of another Value Object or used in wrapping intentions) but is missing the @dataclass decorator.

items.title: Missing Symbol in __all__
items.text: Warns when a public symbol (class, function, or variable) is defined in a module but not included in its __all__ list. Includes a quick-fix to add the symbol to __all__.

items.title: Private Module Import
items.text: Warns when you import symbols from a "private" module (one whose name starts with an underscore). DDD encourages importing through public APIs.

items.title: Shadowing Stdlib Module
items.text: Warns when a project module has the same name as a standard library module, which can lead to confusing import errors.

items.title: Constant is not Final
items.text: Warns when a variable that looks like a constant (uppercase naming) is not annotated with Final.

items.title: Abstract Method Not Implemented
items.text: Ensures all abstract methods are implemented in concrete subclasses.

items.title: Developer remote-control API
items.text:
BetterPy exposes a small HTTP remote-control API for automated debugging in dev builds.

The endpoint is intentionally narrow:

  • Available only when the active release channel is dev.
  • Accepts loopback requests only.
  • Requires a configured token for every endpoint except GET /ping and the bootstrap-only GET /status. status discloses no token value and is limited to connection metadata needed to identify the intended local IDE instance. When both the settings-panel session token and betterpy.remoteControl.token are present, either token is accepted.
  • Uses the X-BetterPy-Remote-Token header, or a token query parameter.

Base URL:

http://127.0.0.1:<IDE built-in server port>/api/betterpy-remote

The IDE built-in server commonly starts at 63342, but that port is not an instance identity. BetterPy writes a non-secret connection profile named betterpy-remote-control.json in the selected IDE configuration directory after a project opens. It contains the effective base URL, endpoint path, instance ID, release channel, and whether a token is configured.

Prefer the lifecycle harness when starting an IDE for automation:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_harness.py start \
  --ide-version 2026.1 \
  --project "$PWD/examples/feature_showcase"
source build/ide-remote-harness/connection.env

It builds current sources, chooses a free port, generates authentication, launches a downloaded platform in the Gradle sandbox, and verifies IDE/plugin runtime identity, including the hash calculated from the loaded plugin JAR. status re-runs diagnostics for the managed session and stop terminates its launcher. Session and environment files under build/ide-remote-harness/ are mode 0600.

Use --ide-build or --ide-path when an installed EAP/nightly is required. These fallback modes deploy into that app's normal configuration. For an IDE that is already running, prefer the profile to guessed ports:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py find-profile
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py \
  --connection-file "$HOME/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.2/betterpy-remote-control.json" \
  doctor

The Copy Connection Environment BetterPy action copies an equivalent shell-safe setup, including the current session token. The profile never contains a token.

find-profile scans standard JetBrains configuration roots, selects the profile with the latest startedAt, and reports ambiguous: true plus every candidate when multiple IDE profiles exist. Always confirm its selected instanceId with wait-ready --expected-instance-id.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
From the repository root, use the harness for a reproducible session:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_harness.py start --ide-version 2026.1 \
  --project "$PWD/examples/feature_showcase"
source build/ide-remote-harness/connection.env
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py action CodeCompletion --wait
python3 scripts/ide_remote_harness.py status
python3 scripts/ide_remote_harness.py stop

doctor first uses tokenless /status or /ping to distinguish a connection failure from a reachable endpoint rejected by its channel, feature, loopback, or token gate. It reports endpoint reachability, token state, channel, feature flag state, project availability, modal blocking, and smart-mode/indexing readiness.

items.title: MCP versus REST and CLI
items.text:
MCP-connected agents can use the focused ide_remote_* toolset without a REST port, connection profile, or token:

  • ide_remote_status
  • ide_remote_open
  • ide_remote_action
  • ide_remote_diagnostics
  • ide_remote_modal and ide_remote_modal_action
  • ide_remote_wait_ready

The tools still require the dev channel, enabled ide-remote-control feature, and an open MCP project. They call the same controller contracts and report stable codes through MCP failures. Waits are interruptible when the MCP request is canceled.

Use MCP for the common status/open/action/diagnostics/modal/readiness workflow. Use REST/CLI for the full-fidelity surface: schema discovery, project pinning, recording, layout and geometry, tool-window trees, pagination loops, feature logging, and streamed multi-step scenarios.

items.title: Installed PyCharm EAP runbook
items.text: Use this runbook when validating a dev BetterPy build inside an installed PyCharm EAP such as 2026.2 EAP.

items.title: 1. Deploy the dev plugin into the installed IDE
items.text:
Run the repository deploy script and select the installed PyCharm EAP from the interactive list:

JAVA_HOME=/Users/jo/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jbr-21.0.10/Contents/Home \
  ./scripts/deploy.sh

The script builds the plugin and installs it into the settings directory used by the selected app. Close the target IDE before deploying so the plugin is loaded cleanly on the next launch.

For unattended deployment, set BETTERPY_DEPLOY_NONINTERACTIVE=true, BETTERPY_REQUIRED_PYCHARM_BUILD, BETTERPY_REMOTE_CONTROL_ENABLED=true, BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN, and BETTERPY_IDE_SERVER_PORT. The script persists the token in both idea.properties and custom pycharm.vmoptions, because a pre-existing VM option overrides the properties file. It never places the token in the launched IDE's process arguments.

items.title: 2. Configure token and port
items.text:
Generate a session token from the BetterPy settings panel, or add the remote-control token and, when needed, the built-in server port to the target IDE idea.properties. For PyCharm 2026.2, the file is typically:

~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.2/idea.properties

Example properties:

betterpy.remoteControl.token=dev-secret
rpc.port=63343

Restart the IDE after changing these properties. A generated session token is shown and copied first in settings, but the JVM-property token remains valid until the property is removed and the IDE is restarted. A configured token is required for every endpoint except GET /ping.

items.title: 3. Launch and point the client at the IDE
items.text:
Open the installed app and export matching client values:

open -a "PyCharm 2026.2 EAP"

export BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN=dev-secret
export BETTERPY_REMOTE_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:63343/api/betterpy-remote
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py doctor --try-ports 63342,63343

The expected doctor result has ready=true, channel=dev, and featureEnabled=true. If ping succeeds but protected endpoints fail, check that BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN matches either the session token shown in settings or the betterpy.remoteControl.token property. Restart the IDE after property changes.

items.title: 4. Open a project and handle trust/modal state
items.text:
Open the project with the IDE UI or launcher. Then inspect modal state through the remote-control API rather than using OS-level automation:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py modal
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-modal --closed --timeout-ms 30000

If a trust dialog or another modal is open, inspect its component tree and click the intended button by stable text/name/accessibility metadata:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py modal
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py modal-action click --text "Trust Project"
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-modal --closed --timeout-ms 30000

Use exact modal output from your IDE when choosing --text, --name, or --accessible-name; do not click unrelated dialogs blindly.

items.title: 5. Wait for a usable IDE
items.text:
After opening and trusting the project, wait for the usual readiness gates with one command:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-ready --timeout-ms 60000 --poll-ms 250

wait-ready retries transient bootstrap connection failures until its deadline. For automation that must avoid controlling a different running IDE, read instanceId from /status and require it explicitly:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-ready \
  --expected-instance-id "<instance-id>" \
  --timeout-ms 60000 --poll-ms 250

If layout stability is not relevant for a headless check, skip that gate:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-ready --skip-layout-stable

items.title: 6. Collect diagnostics and feature logs
items.text:
Open the file under test, wait for smart mode, collect diagnostics, and trigger an action with feature-scoped logging in one action command:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py open tests/test_markers.py --line 12 --column 16
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-smart-mode --timeout-ms 60000
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py diagnostics --path tests/test_markers.py
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py action CodeCompletion \
  --wait \
  --log-feature-id pytest-mark-completion \
  --log-level trace \
  --label marker-completion-smoke

The action result includes the command status and any captured logFiles, so a second manual wait-command call is not needed.

items.title: Web framework discovery diagnostics
items.text:
web-discovery-diagnostics accepts no path, framework, or reset options. It performs one direct all-framework scanner pass for the open project; it is not a cache-hit latency measurement and does not read editor highlighting diagnostics. After doctor supplies the live base URL and wait-ready has completed, invoke it with the configured token:

BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN="$DISCOVERY_TOKEN" \
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py --base "$DISCOVERY_BASE_URL" \
  web-discovery-diagnostics

The successful payload is flattened beneath ok: true and contains:

  • elapsedNanos: elapsed time for the one direct scanner invocation.
  • applications and endpoints: aggregate totals from that invocation.
  • frameworks: one declaration-ordered row for every supported framework, including zero-result frameworks; each row has framework, applications, and endpoints.
  • counters: aggregate scanner measurements only. discoveryRequests counts scanner requests; indexedCandidateLookups and indexedCandidateFiles describe index-based candidate selection; fullPythonScanFallbacks records fallback selection; fullPythonMarkerScanFilesExamined, routeObjectCandidateFiles, and discoveryFiles describe candidate breadth.
  • counters.phaseTimings: a declaration-ordered list containing every phase, including skipped phases with zero timings. Each item has phase, calls, totalNanos, and maxNanos. The phases are DISCOVERY_FILES, FULL_PYTHON_MARKER_SCAN, PSI_EXTRACTION_AND_TYPE_INFERENCE, ENDPOINT_AND_INCLUDE_COLLECTION, INCLUDE_EXPANSION, RESULT_NORMALIZATION, and CONNEXION_OPENAPI_SCAN.

The endpoint returns the normal error envelope, { "ok": false, "error": "..." }, before scanning when either prerequisite fails. The exact errors are:

  • API route navigation is disabled
  • Project is indexing; wait for smart mode before running web discovery diagnostics

items.title: Scenario streaming
items.text:
POST /scenario/run/stream executes the same RemoteScenarioRunRequest accepted by POST /scenario/run, but returns progressive newline-delimited JSON. The response content type is application/x-ndjson; each line is one RemoteStreamEvent object and clients should process lines as they arrive.

The existing buffered scenario endpoint remains unchanged. Use streaming when a live IDE smoke test needs progress feedback, a terminal aggregate result, and feature log file references without manual action → wait → state chaining.

items.title: Event schema
items.text:
Every event has this envelope:

{
  "type": "scenario.step.finished",
  "sequence": 3,
  "timestampMillis": 1761693720000,
  "scenarioId": null,
  "stepIndex": 0,
  "commandId": "cmd-123",
  "label": "marker completion",
  "correlationId": "smoke-1",
  "payload": {}
}
Event type When it appears Payload scenario.started Before the first step is dispatched. Empty in the first implementation wave. scenario.step.started Immediately before a step handler runs. Empty; use stepIndex, label, and correlationId from the envelope. scenario.step.finished After a step returns a successful RemoteScenarioStepResult. The step result object. scenario.step.failed After a step returns a failed result, including assertion or wait mismatches. The failed step result object. logging.files After an action step returns feature-scoped log files. A list of RemoteFeatureLogFile objects. scenario.finished After normal completion or stopOnError termination. The final RemoteScenarioRunResponse. error For parse/access/execution failures handled after the stream route begins. RemoteStreamError with a message and stable code.

Feature log content is intentionally not streamed in this wave. Action steps can still request logs with logFeatureIds and logLevel; streamed logging.files events expose durable log-file references with featureId, category, scopeId, path, and loggerNames. Feature ids resolve to logging categories from feature metadata, and the logging service attaches both plain category logger names and #category logger names.

items.title: CLI stream follow
items.text:
Use scenario-run --stream to print compact NDJSON and exit non-zero when an error event appears or the final scenario.finished payload has passed=false:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py scenario-run --stream --body '{
  "label": "marker completion stream",
  "correlationId": "pytest-marker-stream-smoke",
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "open",
      "label": "open test file",
      "open": {"path": "build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project/tests/test_markers.py"}
    },
    {
      "type": "action",
      "label": "complete marker",
      "action": {
        "actionId": "CodeCompletion",
        "logFeatureIds": ["pytest-mark-completion"],
        "logLevel": "trace"
      }
    }
  ]
}'

Add --pretty for indented event objects while following a stream manually. The default remains one compact JSON object per line for machine consumers.

Use a generic route step when a registered operation has no named scenario step. Existing named steps and aliases remain supported:

{
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "route",
      "route": {"method": "GET", "path": "/projects"}
    }
  ]
}

The optional route.body object is serialized as the request JSON. Failed registered operations preserve their stable code as errorCode on the scenario step result.

Example output:

{"sequence":1,"timestampMillis":1761693720000,"type":"scenario.started"}
{"label":"open test file","sequence":2,"stepIndex":0,"timestampMillis":1761693720001,"type":"scenario.step.started"}
{"label":"open test file","payload":{"index":0,"ok":true,"type":"open"},"sequence":3,"stepIndex":0,"timestampMillis":1761693720002,"type":"scenario.step.finished"}
{"commandId":"cmd-123","label":"complete marker","payload":[{"featureId":"pytest-mark-completion","category":"com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.features.pytestMarkCompletion.PytestMarkCompletionContributor","scopeId":"scope-1","path":"/Users/jo/Library/Logs/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.2/betterpy-remote/...log","loggerNames":["com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.features.pytestMarkCompletion.PytestMarkCompletionContributor","#com.github.chbndrhnns.betterpy.features.pytestMarkCompletion.PytestMarkCompletionContributor"]}],"sequence":6,"stepIndex":1,"timestampMillis":1761693720005,"type":"logging.files"}
{"payload":{"passed":true,"steps":[]},"sequence":7,"timestampMillis":1761693720006,"type":"scenario.finished"}

curl can follow the stream too:

curl -N \
  -H "X-BetterPy-Remote-Token: $BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/x-ndjson" \
  -d '{"steps":[]}' \
  "$BETTERPY_REMOTE_BASE/scenario/run/stream"

items.title: Pytest marker live smoke recipe
items.text: This recipe validates the pytest marker completion and strict-marker diagnostics workflow against a real IDE project. It is designed for a disposable uv-based project outside spec/.

items.title: 1. Create a small uv project
items.text:
mkdir -p build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project/tests
cd build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project
uv init --bare
cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "betterpy-live-pytest-marker-smoke"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
strict_markers = true
markers = [
  "slow: marks slow tests",
  "smoke: marks smoke tests",
]
EOF
uv add --dev pytest
cat > tests/test_markers.py <<'EOF'
import pytest


@pytest.mark.slow
def test_registered_marker():
    assert True


@pytest.mark.unknown_live_marker
def test_unknown_marker():
    assert True
EOF
cd ../../..

items.title: 2. Open, trust, and wait for readiness
items.text:
Open the project in the installed EAP, then handle the trust dialog only through remote-control modal endpoints:

open -a "PyCharm 2026.2 EAP" --args "$PWD/build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project"

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py doctor --try-ports 63342,63343
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py modal
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py modal-action click --text "Trust Project"
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-modal --closed --timeout-ms 30000
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-ready --timeout-ms 60000 --poll-ms 250

If no trust dialog is open, modal-action is not needed; wait-ready should be the next command.

items.title: 3. Check strict-marker diagnostics
items.text:
Open the file and collect diagnostics after smart mode:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py open \
  build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project/tests/test_markers.py \
  --line 9 --column 14
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-smart-mode --timeout-ms 60000
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py diagnostics \
  --path build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project/tests/test_markers.py

Expected result: diagnostics include a PytestStrictMarkersInspection warning for unknown_live_marker, while registered markers such as slow and smoke do not produce BetterPy strict-marker warnings.

items.title: 4. Trigger marker completion with feature logs
items.text:
Add a completion target such as @pytest.mark.smo in a disposable test file, place the caret after smo, and run completion with feature-scoped logging:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py action CodeCompletion \
  --wait \
  --wait-status finished \
  --wait-timeout-ms 10000 \
  --log-feature-id pytest-mark-completion \
  --log-level trace \
  --label pytest-marker-live-smoke

Expected result: the command finishes, the marker completes to smoke, and the JSON output includes logFiles for the pytest-mark-completion feature. Inspect those files if completion candidates are unexpected.

To follow the same flow as a structured stream, run a scenario that requests the same feature logs from the action step:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py scenario-run --stream --body '{
  "label": "pytest marker live smoke",
  "steps": [
    {
      "type": "open",
      "label": "open marker file",
      "open": {
        "path": "build/live-ide-pytest-marker-project/tests/test_markers.py",
        "position": {"line": 9, "column": 14}
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "action",
      "label": "marker completion",
      "action": {
        "actionId": "CodeCompletion",
        "logFeatureIds": ["pytest-mark-completion"],
        "logLevel": "trace"
      }
    }
  ]
}'

Expected result: the stream ends with scenario.finished and includes a logging.files event for pytest-mark-completion. Inspect the referenced paths to review PytestMarkCompletionContributor diagnostics; raw log records are not embedded in the stream.

items.title: Future streaming direction
items.text:
The first streaming wave keeps log delivery to durable file references. If that is not enough, a later additive slice can stream selected log records inline or add a dedicated log-tail endpoint keyed by scopeId or commandId.

flowchart LR
  Scenario[Scenario stream] --> Refs[Log file refs]
  Refs --> Files[Scoped log files]
  CLI[CLI] --> Files
  Future[Future log tail] --> CLI

Keep future log streaming opt-in and scoped to requested logFeatureIds so live validation remains bounded and does not expose unrelated IDE logs.

items.title: Semantic tool-window trees and console output
items.text:
Use the selected content of a named tool window as a semantic automation target:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py tree-state Project --max-nodes 1000
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py tree-select Project Project src main.py --tree-id tree-0
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py console-output Run --max-chars 100000

tree-state returns visible JTree components in deterministic component order. Each materialized node includes its full ancestor-to-node semanticPath, label, selection, expansion, visibility, leaf status, and child count. Collapsed tree models may not have loaded remote or lazy descendants; only children currently materialized by the Swing model are returned. --max-nodes accepts 1..10000. When more nodes exist, the response sets truncated: true.

tree-select requires the exact full semantic path. It expands materialized ancestors, selects and reveals one match, focuses the tree, and returns refreshed tree state. Missing and duplicate paths fail without changing the current selection. When several trees are visible, use the returned tree-<index> value with --tree-id, or use --component-name; missing or duplicate selectors fail instead of choosing the first component.

console-output reads one visible Swing text component or IntelliJ editor-backed component, normalizes line endings to \n, and reports totalChars plus truncated. --max-chars accepts 1..1000000. When several readable sources are visible, select one with its returned source-<index> via --source-id or with --component-name. Hidden sources are ignored; absent, missing-selector, and ambiguous-selector cases return explicit errors.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Likely cause Next step Connection refused IDE is not running, the built-in server is on another port, or BETTERPY_REMOTE_BASE points to the wrong IDE. Run doctor --try-ports 63342,63343, or pass the target IDE's --connection-file; start the IDE or set rpc.port. 401 or token error Client token is missing or does not match any configured settings/JVM token. Export BETTERPY_REMOTE_TOKEN, use Copy Connection Environment, or update idea.properties and restart the IDE. ping/status works but state fails Bootstrap endpoints are intentionally tokenless; protected endpoints require a token. Provide the token for all other commands. channel is not dev The target IDE loaded a non-dev plugin build. Deploy a dev-channel build into the installed IDE. featureEnabled=false The remote-control feature is disabled or filtered out. Verify the dev feature set and plugin deployment. Commands stay queued A modal is open, the IDE is indexing, or the command was not followed to completion. Run doctor, handle modal state, then use action --wait or wait-command. Modal blocked Trust or another IDE dialog is waiting for a user decision. Inspect with modal, act with modal-action, then wait-modal --closed. Dumb mode/indexing Project indexes are not ready. Run wait-ready --timeout-ms 60000 or wait-smart-mode --timeout-ms 60000. Diagnostics are empty File is not open/highlighted yet, the inspection is disabled, or project trust/indexing is incomplete. Open the file, wait for readiness, then call diagnostics again. 409 with UNSAVED_DOCUMENT A remote file/write would overwrite unsaved open-editor changes. Save or discard the local editor changes, then retry; BetterPy does not silently replace them.

items.title: Project lifecycle
items.text:
Use project-close to close and dispose one currently open project. Select it with exactly one of --name or --path; names must be unambiguous, while paths must exactly match the base path returned by project-list. Native IntelliJ save prompts and close vetoes are preserved. If the closed project was pinned, the pin is cleared automatically.

Use project-open --path <absolute-path> to load an existing IntelliJ project from disk. The path must be an absolute existing directory, and the request is rejected if that project is already open. The lifecycle service temporarily adds the normalized path to IntelliJ's trusted-path list while loading, then removes only the entry it added. It also disables the IDE's application-exit confirmation for the automation session. Opening does not pin the project.

Both commands return only after IntelliJ reports the close or open operation as completed. Opening completion does not mean indexing is finished; follow it with wait-ready or wait-smart-mode before project-model or PSI operations:

project=/absolute/path/to/existing-project
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-close --path "$project"
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-list
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-open --path "$project"
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py wait-ready --timeout-ms 60000 --poll-ms 250

The lifecycle routes are protected but do not require a currently resolved project. Consequently, closing the last project leaves the same IDE instance reachable on the Welcome screen, and project-open can recover it using the same connection environment and token. Lifecycle routes are intentionally not available inside scenario-run, because closing its owning project would invalidate scenario state.

items.title: Response semantics
items.text:
Buffered JSON endpoints return an additive error envelope with ok: false, the existing human-readable error message, and a stable machine-readable code. Streaming failures expose the same code in RemoteStreamError. Clients should branch on code, not message text. Older servers may omit code; the CLI keeps the legacy generic failure exit for those responses.

Status Meaning 400 Bad Request Invalid arguments or request payload. 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid remote-control token. 403 Forbidden Channel, feature-enabled, or loopback gate rejected the request. 404 Not Found Unsupported remote-control endpoint. 409 Conflict Current IDE state prevents the operation, such as an unsaved-document conflict, duplicate project open, close veto, or platform lifecycle failure. 504 Gateway Timeout A bounded remote-control operation timed out. 500 Internal Server Error An unexpected server failure occurred. Code Category CLI exit CONNECTION_ERROR The CLI could not connect to the IDE. This code is client-generated. 10 CHANNEL_NOT_DEV, FEATURE_DISABLED, LOOPBACK_REQUIRED, TOKEN_NOT_CONFIGURED, TOKEN_MISSING, TOKEN_INVALID Availability or authentication gate rejected the request. 11 TIMEOUT Client transport or bounded server operation timed out. 12 UNSUPPORTED_ROUTE, VALIDATION_ERROR The route or request is invalid. 13 CONFLICT, UNSAVED_DOCUMENT Current IDE state conflicts with the operation. 14 INTERNAL_ERROR The server failed unexpectedly. 15

Successful commands exit 0. Unknown codes and error responses from older servers exit 2 for backward compatibility.

items.title: Wait execution and pagination
items.text:
Buffered wait/*, action, scenario/run, and project lifecycle requests execute on a bounded background pool rather than an IDE built-in-server worker. Responses are marshaled back to the request channel, and closing the channel cancels the polling task. Existing timeout and JSON semantics are unchanged; ping, status, and other short requests remain responsive while waits are pending.

POST /tool-windows/{id}/trees, POST /usages, and POST /diagnostics accept optional limit and opaque cursor fields. A limited response includes nextCursor while more ordered results remain and keeps the existing truncated signal. Follow pages until nextCursor is absent:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py usages --path src/example.py --limit 100
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py usages --path src/example.py \
  --limit 100 --cursor '<nextCursor>'

Cursors bind to the request’s stable filters and cannot be reused with another path, position, tree selector, or inspection filter. Malformed, mismatched, and out-of-range cursors return VALIDATION_ERROR. Omitting both pagination fields preserves the legacy bounded response behavior.

items.title: Recording crop workflow
items.text:
Use typed project commands before a longer workflow when several projects are open:

python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-list
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-pin --path "$PWD/examples/betterpy_showcase"
# run the workflow
python3 scripts/ide_remote_control.py project-unpin

The typed recording-start, recording-sample, recording-stop, and recording-reset commands map directly to the /recording/* routes. The recording lab remains the preferred orchestrator for repeatable video capture.

Coordinates returned by geometry endpoints are physical screen coordinates, intended for post-processing screen recordings. For a full-IDE crop:

python scripts/ide_remote_control.py window-bounds --width 1280 --height 720
python scripts/ide_remote_control.py occupied-start --scope all --session-id demo --auto-sample-actions --sample-interval-ms 250
# run the scripted interaction here
python scripts/ide_remote_control.py occupied-stop demo --margin 16 --ffmpeg-crop --even-dimensions

Use --scope editor when the final crop should include only the selected editor content area, --scope ide for the IDE frame, and --scope all for the union of visible IDE-owned windows such as popups, dialogs, and floating windows. Balloon notifications are excluded by default because they often appear in the bottom-right corner and inflate recording size; pass --include-balloons when they are part of the scenario.

The returned bounds is the union of all sampled bounds in the session; margin expands that final rectangle after sampling. --auto-sample-actions samples after remote-control operations such as open, actions, gutter actions, inlay actions, modal actions, tool-window changes, and layout presets. --sample-interval-ms adds timer-based sampling while the session is active, which helps catch short-lived popups.

For deterministic recording setup, layout-preset can set window bounds, hide tool windows, focus the editor, and configure individual tool windows:

python scripts/ide_remote_control.py layout-preset \
  --width 1280 --height 720 \
  --hide-tool-windows \
  --focus-editor \
  --tool-window '{"id":"Pytest Explorer","visible":true,"anchor":"right","width":420}'

screenshot-crop is an opt-in prototype that screenshots the selected geometry bounds and computes a non-background crop using the top-left pixel as the background reference.

Modal actions can target controls by path, name, accessibleName, exact text, textContains, type, and className. Prefer name or accessibleName when available because positional paths change when dialog layouts change.

items.title: Feature Logging
items.text:
POST /logging accepts:

{
  "featureIds": ["parameter-object-refactoring"],
  "enabled": true,
  "level": "trace",
  "scopeId": "repro-1"
}

level can be debug, trace, or all. scopeId is optional; when omitted, the IDE generates one. This is runtime-only logging capture: feature ids are resolved through feature metadata, and the returned feature/file category values come from each feature's loggingCategories. The response includes logFiles with exact paths under the IDE log directory.

POST /action also accepts logFeatureIds and logLevel. In that mode, logging is scoped to the command id, enabled while the action runs, disabled afterwards, and the same logFiles are returned in both the action response and command snapshot.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
• Target areas: core/*, features/pytest/**, features/searcheverywhere/**, features/parameterObject/mcp/**.
  • Risk classes: wrong SDK selection, wrong root/path resolution, scope leakage across attached directories, UI/context ambiguity.
  • Baseline behavior expectation: module/file/content-root-aware behavior first, explicit project-wide fallback only when intended.

items.title: Risk matrix
items.text: Priority Risk type Hotspot (file:line) User-visible multi-project failure mode Recommended fix strategy P0 Wrong SDK core/python/PythonVersionGuard.kt:42-47 Feature gating can report unsupported Python version based on an unrelated attached module because first module SDK is used as fallback. Introduce context-aware SDK resolver (VirtualFile/PsiElement/Module first), with explicit project-only fallback. P0 Wrong SDK core/services/PythonStdlibService.kt:20-23 Stdlib symbol resolution may use wrong interpreter paths, causing missing/incorrect results in mixed-interpreter windows. Route through shared SDK resolver; require anchor context when available. P0 Wrong SDK core/actions/CopyDiagnosticDataAction.kt:42-46 Diagnostics can show the wrong interpreter, misleading bug reports and support data in multi-project windows. Resolve SDK from selected file/editor context; fallback to project-only explicitly. P0 Wrong SDK features/pytest/explorer/collection/PytestCollectorTask.kt:105-107 Pytest collection command can run with the wrong interpreter, yielding empty/incorrect test trees. Resolve SDK per collection root/module; include selected file/module context in collector task inputs. P0 Wrong root/path features/pytest/explorer/collection/PytestCollectorTask.kt:58-62 Relative module paths become invalid when the active test file lives outside project.basePath root in attached directories. Compute relative paths from the file’s content root (ProjectFileIndex) instead of project.basePath. P0 Wrong root/path features/pytest/explorer/trigger/PytestExplorerStartupActivity.kt:190-196,214-236 Discovery trigger skips or mis-targets tests in non-base attached roots. Build collection targets from indexed content roots/modules; keep project-level trigger as deliberate fallback. P0 Wrong root/path features/pytest/explorer/ui/PytestExplorerPanel.kt:427,590-646 Refresh, follow-caret, scope-to-file, and file-presence checks can map to wrong test nodes or miss tests in attached roots. Convert all path mapping to content-root-relative identities; pass module/root identity through tree model. P0 Wrong root/path features/pytest/explorer/ui/PytestFixtureExplorerPanel.kt:197-204,433 Fixture navigation and refresh context can open wrong files or fail for non-base attached roots. Resolve fixture file identity by content root/module context; avoid base-path string stripping. P0 Wrong root/path features/pytest/explorer/psi/PytestPsiResolver.kt:164-171 PSI resolution first tries project.basePath and misses attached-root files; fallback can pick ambiguous same-name files. Resolve via content roots and module-aware candidate narrowing before filename index fallback. P0 Wrong root/path features/parameterObject/mcp/ParameterObjectToolset.kt:116-117,241-242 MCP tools reject valid files or mutate wrong files when pathInProject is interpreted against only project.basePath. Accept paths relative to active content root/module (or workspace root list); disambiguate by module/root id when needed. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureFindUsagesHandlerFactory.kt:95 Find usages can mix fixture parameters from unrelated attached directories with same names. Default to anchor-derived suggestion scope (PySearchUtilBase.defaultSuggestionScope(anchor)), optional explicit project-wide mode. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureUnusedInspection.kt:86 Fixtures may be considered “used” due to matches in unrelated attached directories, masking true unused warnings. Narrow scope to fixture anchor/module root; broaden only for explicitly project-wide inspections. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/inlinefixture/InlineFixtureAnalyzer.kt:143 Inline fixture analysis can pick usages from other attached directories, causing unsafe transformations. Restrict search scope to resolved fixture chain roots and anchor file/module scope. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureRenameProcessor.kt:163 Rename may update parameters/usages outside intended project root when names collide. Use context-bounded scope with explicit user choice for broadened refactor. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/hooks/PytestHookLineMarkerProvider.kt:50 Hook implementation gutter navigation includes unrelated conftest.py files from attached directories. Scope by current file/module roots first; optionally expose “search all attached roots”. P1 Scope leakage features/searcheverywhere/PytestIdentifierResolver.kt:28 Identifier resolution returns ambiguous matches across attached roots with same file names. Include root/module identity in match ranking and prefer current context root. P1 Scope leakage features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureResolver.kt:874 Fixture chain resolution can cross directory boundaries unexpectedly, producing incorrect parent/override chains. Add root-aware boundary checks to resolver traversal with explicit cross-root mode. P1 Wrong root/path features/searcheverywhere/PytestTestsContributor.kt:68-70 Search Everywhere fallback opens wrong file when identical relative paths exist in attached roots. Replace base-path fallback with resolver that uses snapshot root metadata + module context. P1 Wrong root/path features/searcheverywhere/PytestFixturesContributor.kt:73-75 Fixture result navigation may fail or jump to wrong root due to base-path-only concatenation. Navigate through PytestPsiResolver using root-aware file identity first; fallback by scoped candidate matching.

items.title: Cross-cutting remediation rules
items.text:
1. Canonical context resolution order:
  2. Active PsiElement / selected VirtualFile / editor context
  3. Owning module/content root
  4. Explicit project-only fallback (for misc/project-only contexts)
  5. Path identities:
  6. Stop encoding identity as project.basePath-relative string alone.
  7. Carry {contentRootId, relativePath} or equivalent through pytest snapshot/navigation flows.
  8. Search policy:
  9. Treat project-wide scope as opt-in behavior; default to anchor-derived scope.
  10. SDK policy:
  11. Replace first-module fallback with shared SDK resolver that supports both module and project-only contexts.

items.title: Implementation order recommendation
items.text:
1. P0 foundation: shared context/SKD/root resolution helpers in core/*.
  2. P0 pytest explorer/resolver: collection, startup, explorer panels, PSI resolver.
  3. P1 search/refactor correctness: fixture resolver/rename/inline/find usages/inspection scope tightening.
  4. P1 UX integrations: Search Everywhere contributors, hook gutter navigation, MCP parameter-object path handling.

items.title: Step 2 validation snapshots (expected vs actual)
items.text:
• PytestPsiResolverTest.testResolveFixtureWithDuplicateRelativePathAcrossRootsIsAmbiguous
  • Expected (multi-project-safe): resolver should require root/module disambiguation.
  • Actual (current): resolver returns one arbitrary candidate when two roots contain tests/conftest.py.
  • PytestPsiResolverTest.testResolveTestWithDuplicateRelativeModulePathAcrossRootsIsAmbiguous
  • Expected: duplicate tests/test_api.py::test_dupe should be root-aware, not first-match.
  • Actual: resolver returns one match from either root without explicit context.
  • PytestIdentifierResolverTest.testResolveWithDuplicateRelativePathAcrossRootsIsAmbiguous
  • Expected: identifier resolution should prioritize current root/module (or return ambiguity).
  • Actual: returns a function from either root for identical relative path identifiers.
  • CopyDiagnosticDataActionTest.testGetPythonInterpreterVersionWithNullProjectReturnsUnknown
  • Expected: project-only/misc context behaves explicitly (no fake module inference).
  • Actual: returns Unknown, confirming explicit fallback path exists for no-context mode.

items.title: Group A — Core context + SDK resolution (P0)
items.text:
• Add shared context object (example shape: ResolutionContext(project, psi, virtualFile, module, contentRoot)) and a single resolver API under core/*.
  • Replace first-module fallbacks at:
  • core/python/PythonVersionGuard.kt:42-47
  • core/services/PythonStdlibService.kt:20-23
  • core/actions/CopyDiagnosticDataAction.kt:42-46
  • features/pytest/explorer/collection/PytestCollectorTask.kt:105-107
  • features/pytest/explorer/ui/PytestFixtureExplorerPanel.kt:412-414
  • features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureResolver.kt:549-552
  • Fallback policy:
  • file/editor/module-aware SDK,
  • content-root/module default SDK,
  • explicit project-only fallback (Unknown/no-op where appropriate).

items.title: Group B — Root-aware pytest collection/navigation (P0)
items.text:
• Replace base-path-relative identity with root-aware identity ({contentRootId, relativePath}) in explorer collection + tree mapping.
  • Update hotspots:
  • features/pytest/explorer/collection/PytestCollectorTask.kt:58-62
  • features/pytest/explorer/trigger/PytestExplorerStartupActivity.kt:190-196,214-236
  • features/pytest/explorer/ui/PytestExplorerPanel.kt:427,590-646
  • features/pytest/explorer/ui/PytestFixtureExplorerPanel.kt:197-204,433
  • features/pytest/explorer/psi/PytestPsiResolver.kt:164-171
  • Enforce deterministic disambiguation rules:
  • prefer active file/module root;
  • if still ambiguous, surface explicit ambiguity instead of arbitrary candidate.

items.title: Group C — Scope tightening for fixtures/search/refactor (P1)
items.text:
• Default search scopes to anchor-derived scope and use project-wide only when user intent is global.
  • Update hotspots:
  • features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureFindUsagesHandlerFactory.kt:95
  • features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureUnusedInspection.kt:86
  • features/pytest/inlinefixture/InlineFixtureAnalyzer.kt:143
  • features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureRenameProcessor.kt:163
  • features/pytest/hooks/PytestHookLineMarkerProvider.kt:50
  • features/searcheverywhere/PytestIdentifierResolver.kt:28
  • features/pytest/fixture/PytestFixtureResolver.kt:874

items.title: Group D — Search Everywhere + MCP path context (P1)
items.text:
• Replace project.basePath concatenation in Search Everywhere contributors with root-aware resolver calls.
  • Update:
  • features/searcheverywhere/PytestTestsContributor.kt:68-70
  • features/searcheverywhere/PytestFixturesContributor.kt:73-75
  • Extend MCP pathInProject contract to accept/resolve content-root context; disambiguate duplicate relative paths before read/write ops.
  • features/parameterObject/mcp/ParameterObjectToolset.kt:116-117,241-242

items.title: Implementation checkpoints and regression coverage
items.text:
1. Checkpoint A (core helpers merged)
  2. New/updated tests for SDK/context resolver behavior in module-aware and project-only contexts.
  3. Checkpoint B (pytest explorer + resolver migrated)
  4. Keep ambiguity repro tests green and change expected behavior from arbitrary resolution to deterministic/explicit ambiguity.
  5. Run: PytestCollectorTaskTest, PytestPsiResolverTest.
  6. Checkpoint C (scope tightening merged)
  7. Add/adjust fixture usage/rename/inspection tests to prove no cross-root leakage by default.
  8. Run related fixture resolver/rename/inspection suites.
  9. Checkpoint D (search contributors + MCP merged)
  10. Add tests for duplicate relative path IDs and root-aware selection in Search Everywhere + MCP tool path resolution.
  11. Run: PytestIdentifierResolverTest and MCP toolset tests.

Single-project regression requirement for each checkpoint: - Existing single-root behavior must remain unchanged (all pre-existing relevant suites passing), while multi-root ambiguity cases no longer resolve arbitrarily.

items.title: Pytest Release Promotion Implementation Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Promote the approved conservative pytest feature batch to the stable release channel and verify release guards.

Architecture: Stable release inclusion is controlled by the explicit YAML allowlist in src/main/resources/feature-sets/stable.yaml. A focused feature-set test will lock the approved pytest stable feature IDs so future edits cannot accidentally drop or add candidates outside the release decision.

Tech Stack: Kotlin/JUnit 4 tests through Gradle, IntelliJ Platform plugin XML/resource generation, YAML feature-set manifests, Python docs build through uv.

        "pytest-fixture-documentation",

        "pytest-fixture-uninjected-reference-inspection",

        "pytest-identifier-search-everywhere",

        "pytest-plugins-in-non-root-conftest-inspection",
        "pytest-redundant-fixture-import-inspection",
        "pytest-usefixtures-on-fixture-noop-inspection",
        "run-with-debug-logging",
        "surround-with-pytest-raises",
        "toggle-pytest-skip",
        "toggle-pytest-skip-from-test-tree",
    )
    val excludedPytestFeatures = setOf(
        "extract-pytest-fixture",
        "inline-pytest-fixture",
        "pull-up-pytest-fixture",
        "push-down-pytest-fixture",

    assertTrue("stable.yaml is missing approved pytest feature IDs: $missing", missing.isEmpty())
    assertTrue("stable.yaml includes pytest features that should remain held back: $unexpected", unexpected.isEmpty())
